sentences.zh: 嘉靖改元，帝欲尊所生為帝後。

translations.literal: When the Jiajing reign began, the emperor wished to honor his biological parents as emperor and empress.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jiajing reign, the emperor wished to elevate his biological parents to imperial rank.

sentences.zh: 會掖庭火，廷臣多言咎在「大禮」。

translations.literal: Just then there was a fire in the inner palace quarters, and many court officials said the blame lay in the "Great Rites."
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out in the palace women's quarters, many officials at court said the cause was the Great Rites controversy.

sentences.zh: 繼曾亦言：「去年五月日精門災，今月二日長安榜廊災，及今郊祀日，內廷小房又災。

translations.literal: Jiceng also said: "Last May there was disaster at the Gate of Solar Essence; on the second day of this month fire struck the Chang'an bulletin corridor; and on this day of suburban sacrifice, small rooms in the inner court burned again.
translations.idiomatic: Jiceng also memorialized: "Last May the Gate of Solar Essence was stricken; on the second of this month the Chang'an bulletin corridor burned; and today, the day of the suburban sacrifice, small chambers in the inner court have burned again.

sentences.zh: 天有五行，火實主禮。

translations.literal: Heaven has the five phases; fire indeed governs ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has the five phases, and fire is what governs ritual.

sentences.zh: 人有五事，火實主言。

translations.literal: Man has the five affairs; fire indeed governs speech.
translations.idiomatic: Man has the five affairs, and fire is what governs speech.

sentences.zh: 名不正則言不順，言不順則禮不興。

translations.literal: If names are not correct, speech is not in order; if speech is not in order, ritual does not flourish.
translations.idiomatic: When names are not correct, speech is not in order; when speech is not in order, ritual cannot flourish.

sentences.zh: 今歲未期而災者三，廢禮失言之郊也。」

translations.literal: Before the year is out, disasters have thrice occurred—this is abandoning ritual and neglecting speech at the suburban sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Before the year has ended, disaster has come three times—this is ritual abandoned and speech neglected at the suburban sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 提督三千營廣寧伯劉佶久病，繼曾論罷之。

translations.literal: The commandant of the Three Thousand Barracks, Liu Ji, Earl of Guangning, had long been ill; Jiceng memorialized for his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant of the Three Thousand Barracks, Liu Ji, Earl of Guangning, had long been ill, and Jiceng argued that he should be removed.

sentences.zh: 宣大、關陜、廣西數有警，中原盜竊發。

translations.literal: Xuan-Da, Guan-Shaan, and Guangxi repeatedly had alarms; banditry broke out in the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: There were repeated alarms on the Xuan-Da, Guan-Shaan, and Guangxi fronts, and banditry erupted in the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 繼曾陳戰守方略及儲將練兵足食之計，多議行。

translations.literal: Jiceng set forth strategies for offense and defense and plans to store grain, train troops, and keep the army supplied; many of his proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiceng laid out strategies for war and defense and plans to stock provisions, train troops, and keep the army fed; many of his proposals were put into practice.

sentences.zh: 三年，帝漸疏大臣，政率內決。

translations.literal: In the third year, the emperor gradually kept his distance from grand ministers; government affairs were largely decided within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his reign, the emperor grew increasingly distant from senior ministers, and policy was largely decided within the palace.

sentences.zh: 繼曾抗章曰：「比來中旨，大戾王言。

translations.literal: Jiceng submitted a forthright memorial saying: "Of late, edicts from within have greatly violated the kingly way of speech.
translations.idiomatic: Jiceng submitted a bold memorial: "Recently, edicts issued from within have gravely violated the kingly way of speech.

sentences.zh: 事不考經，文不會理，悅邪說之諂媚則賜敕褒俞，惡師保之抗言則漸將放黜。

translations.literal: Matters are not examined against the classics; writings do not accord with reason. If one delights in the flattery of heterodox doctrines, an edict of praise is bestowed; if one hates the forthright words of teachers and protectors, one is gradually to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Matters are not checked against the classics, and documents do not accord with reason. Those who please with heterodox flattery receive edicts of praise, while those who speak out as teachers and protectors are gradually cast aside.

sentences.zh: 臣目睹出涕，口誦吞聲。

translations.literal: Your subject has seen it with his own eyes and wept; he recites it with choked voice.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen it with my own eyes and wept; I speak of it with a choked voice.

sentences.zh: 夫祖宗以來，凡有批答，必付內閣擬進者，非止慮獨見之或偏，亦防矯偽者之假托也。

translations.literal: Since the founding ancestors, whenever there has been a written response, it has always been submitted to the Grand Secretariat for drafting—this was not only to guard against partiality in a single view, but also to guard against impostors who might forge documents.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding ancestors, every written response has been sent to the Grand Secretariat for drafting—not only to guard against the bias of a single view, but also to prevent forgers from passing off false documents.

sentences.zh: 正德之世，蓋極弊矣，尚未有如今日之可駭可嘆者。

translations.literal: The Zhengde era was indeed utterly corrupt, yet there was nothing so horrifying and lamentable as today.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhengde era was corrupt to the utmost, yet there was nothing so horrifying and lamentable as what we see today.

sentences.zh: 左右群小，目不知書，身未經事，乘隙招權，弄筆取寵，故言出無稽，一至於此。

translations.literal: The petty men at the emperor's side do not know books and have never experienced affairs; seizing openings they gather power, wielding the brush to win favor—thus their words are baseless, reaching this extreme.
translations.idiomatic: The petty men at your side cannot read, have never handled affairs, seize every opening to grasp power, and wield the brush to win favor—so their words are baseless, and matters have come to this pass.

sentences.zh: 陛下不與大臣共政，而倚信群小，臣恐大器之不安也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not govern together with grand ministers but relies on petty men; your subject fears that the great vessel will not be secure."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not govern with your grand ministers but trusts petty men; I fear the great vessel of state will not stand secure."

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝震怒，下詔獄掠治，謫金壇縣丞。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was greatly enraged; he sent him to the imperial prison for torture and punishment, and demoted him to assistant magistrate of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was furious; he had Jiceng thrown into the imperial prison for torture and demoted to assistant magistrate of Jintan.

sentences.zh: 給事中張逵、韓楷、鄭一鵬，御史林有孚、馬明衡、季本皆論救，不報。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Zhang Kui, Han Kai, and Zheng Yipeng, and the censors Lin Youfu, Ma Mingheng, and Ji Ben all memorialized in his defense; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries Zhang Kui, Han Kai, and Zheng Yipeng, and the censors Lin Youfu, Ma Mingheng, and Ji Ben all pleaded for him, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 累遷至徽州知府，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to prefect of Huizhou, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to prefect of Huizhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 帝初踐阼，言路大開。

translations.literal: When the emperor first ascended the throne, the avenue of remonstrance was widely opened.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first took the throne, the avenue of remonstrance stood wide open.

sentences.zh: 進言者或過於切直，帝亦優容之。

translations.literal: Those who spoke forth sometimes went too far in bluntness, yet the emperor also treated them with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Some who spoke out were excessively blunt, yet the emperor bore with them.

sentences.zh: 自劉最及繼曾得罪後，厭薄言官，廢黜相繼，納諫之風微矣。

translations.literal: After Liu Zui and Jiceng were punished, the emperor grew weary of and slighted remonstrating officials; dismissals followed one after another, and the spirit of accepting admonition faded.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Zui and Jiceng were punished, the emperor grew weary of remonstrating officials; dismissals followed in succession, and the spirit of heeding counsel waned.

sentences.zh: 最，字振廷，崇仁人。

translations.literal: Zui, style Zhenting, was a native of Chongren.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zui, styled Zhenting, came from Chongren.

sentences.zh: 繼曾同年進士。

translations.literal: He and Jiceng were jinshi in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jiceng passed the jinshi examination in the same year.

sentences.zh: 由慈利知縣入為禮科給事中。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Cili he entered office as supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites section.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from magistrate of Cili to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites section.

sentences.zh: 世宗議定策功，大行封拜，最疏止之。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor deliberated rewards for those who had settled the succession, he carried out extensive enfeoffments and appointments; Zui memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizong Emperor deliberated rewards for settling the succession, he carried out extensive enfeoffments and appointments; Zui memorialized to halt them.

sentences.zh: 尋請帝勤聖學，於宮中日誦《大學衍義》，勿令左右近習誘以匪僻。

translations.literal: Soon he asked the emperor to apply himself to sagely learning, reciting daily in the palace the Extensions of the Great Learning, and not to let those close at hand lead him astray with improper ways.
translations.idiomatic: He soon urged the emperor to devote himself to sagely learning, reciting daily in the palace the Extensions of the Great Learning, and not to let those close at hand lead him astray with improper ways.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，中官崔文以禱祠事誘帝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, the eunuch Cui Wen tempted the emperor with matters of prayer and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing, the eunuch Cui Wen tempted the emperor with prayer and sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 最極言其非，且奏文耗帑金狀。

translations.literal: Zui spoke forcefully against this and also memorialized on Wen's squandering of treasury funds.
translations.idiomatic: Zui spoke out forcefully against this and also memorialized on Wen's squandering of treasury funds.

sentences.zh: 而帝從文言，命最自核侵耗數。

translations.literal: But the emperor followed Wen's words and ordered Zui himself to verify the amount of embezzlement and waste.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor followed Wen's account and ordered Zui himself to verify the amount of embezzlement and waste.

sentences.zh: 最言：「帑銀屬內府，雖計臣不得稽贏縮。

translations.literal: Zui said: "Treasury silver belongs to the inner palace; even the minister of revenue may not audit surplus and deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Zui said: "Treasury silver belongs to the inner palace; even the minister of revenue may not audit surplus and deficit.

sentences.zh: 文乃欲假難行事，逃己罪，制言官」。

translations.literal: Wen now wishes to use difficulty in execution to escape his own crime and restrain remonstrating officials."
translations.idiomatic: Wen now wishes to use difficulty in execution to escape his own crime and restrain remonstrating officials."

sentences.zh: 疏入，忤旨，出為廣德州判官。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it offended the imperial will; he was sent out as assistant magistrate of Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, it offended the emperor; he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 言官論救，不納。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials pleaded for him; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials pleaded for him, but the emperor would not relent.

sentences.zh: 已而東廠太監芮景賢奏最在途仍故銜，乘巨舫，取夫役，巡鹽御史黃國用復遣牌送之。

translations.literal: Before long the Eastern Depot eunuch Rui Jingxian memorialized that Zui on the road still used his former title, rode a great barge, took corvée laborers, and the salt-inspecting censor Huang Guoyong again sent a placard to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Eastern Depot eunuch Rui Jingxian reported that on the road Zui still used his former title, traveled on a great barge, took corvée laborers, and the salt-inspecting censor Huang Guoyong again sent a placard to escort him.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，逮二人下詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and had both men arrested and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and had both men arrested and sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 最充軍邵武，國用謫極邊雜職。

translations.literal: Zui was sentenced to military exile at Shaowu; Guoyong was demoted to a miscellaneous post on the farthest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Zui was sentenced to military exile at Shaowu; Guoyong was demoted to a minor post on the farthest frontier.

sentences.zh: 法司及言官救之，責以黨比。

translations.literal: The judicial offices and remonstrating officials pleaded for them; they were charged with factional collusion.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices and remonstrating officials pleaded for them; they were charged with factional collusion.

sentences.zh: 最居戍所，久之赦還。

translations.literal: Zui dwelt at his place of exile; after a long time he was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zui lived at his place of exile; after a long time he was pardoned and returned.

sentences.zh: 家居二十余年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for more than twenty years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for more than twenty years before he died.

sentences.zh: 朱淛，字必東，莆田人。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhe, style Bidong, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhe, styled Bidong, came from Putian.

sentences.zh: 舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: He placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年成進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 明年春與同縣馬明衡並授御史。

translations.literal: The next spring he and Ma Mingheng of the same county were both appointed censors.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he and Ma Mingheng of the same county were both appointed censors.

sentences.zh: 甫閱月，會昭聖皇太后生辰，有旨免命婦朝賀。

translations.literal: Barely a month had passed when it happened to be the birthday of the Empress Dowager Zhaosheng; an edict exempted titled ladies from court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month had passed when it was the birthday of the Empress Dowager Zhaosheng; an edict exempted titled ladies from attending court to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 淛言：「皇太后親挈神器以授陛下，母子至情，天日昭鑒。

translations.literal: Zhe said: "The empress dowager personally brought the sacred vessel to invest Your Majesty—mother and son share the utmost affection, clear as heaven and sun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe said: "The empress dowager personally brought the sacred vessel to invest Your Majesty—mother and son share the utmost affection, clear as heaven and sun.

sentences.zh: 若傳免朝賀，何以慰親心而隆孝治？」

translations.literal: If it is announced that court congratulations are waived, how can the mother's heart be comforted and filial governance be exalted?"
translations.idiomatic: If it is announced that court congratulations are waived, how can her heart be comforted and filial governance be exalted?"

sentences.zh: 明衡亦言：「暫免朝賀，在恒時則可，在議禮紛更之時則不可。

translations.literal: Mingheng also said: "A temporary waiver of court congratulations may be acceptable in ordinary times, but not when ritual deliberations are in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Mingheng also said: "A temporary waiver of court congratulations may be acceptable in ordinary times, but not when ritual deliberations are in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 且前者興國太后令節，朝賀如儀，今相去不過數旬，而彼此情文互異。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the former festival day of the Empress Dowager of Xingguo, congratulations were conducted according to ritual; now barely several tens of days have passed, yet the emotional and ritual expressions differ from one another.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at the former festival day of the Empress Dowager of Xingguo, congratulations were conducted according to ritual; now barely several tens of days have passed, yet the emotional and ritual expressions differ from one another.

sentences.zh: 詔旨一出，臣民駭疑。

translations.literal: Once an edict is issued, officials and people are shocked and doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Once an edict is issued, officials and people are shocked and doubtful.

sentences.zh: 萬一因禮儀末節，稍成嫌隙，俾陛下貽譏天下，匪細故也。」

translations.literal: If by chance, because of a minor point of ritual, a slight rift should arise, causing Your Majesty to incur ridicule throughout the realm—this is no small matter."
translations.idiomatic: If by chance, because of a minor point of ritual, a slight rift should arise, causing Your Majesty to incur ridicule throughout the realm—this is no small matter."

sentences.zh: 時帝亟欲尊所生，而群臣必欲帝母昭聖，相持未決。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor urgently wished to honor his biological parents, while the officials insisted that the emperor's mother was Zhaosheng; the standoff was unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor urgently wished to honor his biological parents, while the officials insisted that the emperor's mother was Zhaosheng; the standoff remained unresolved.

sentences.zh: 二人疏入，帝恚且怒。

translations.literal: When the two men's memorials entered, the emperor was resentful and angry.
translations.idiomatic: When the two men's memorials arrived, the emperor was resentful and furious.

sentences.zh: 立捕至內廷，責以離間宮闈，歸過於上，下詔獄拷訊。

translations.literal: He immediately had them seized and brought to the inner court, charged with sowing discord in the palace, and with shifting blame onto the sovereign; they were sent to the imperial prison for torture and interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately had them seized and brought to the inner court, charged with sowing discord in the palace and shifting blame onto the sovereign; they were sent to the imperial prison for torture and interrogation.

sentences.zh: 侍郎何孟春、御史蕭一中論救，皆不聽。

translations.literal: The vice minister He Mengchun and the censor Xiao Yizhong pleaded for them; all were ignored.
translations.idiomatic: The vice minister He Mengchun and the censor Xiao Yizhong pleaded for them, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 御史陳逅、季本、員外郎林應驄繼諫。

translations.literal: The censors Chen Hou and Ji Ben and the bureau director Lin Yingcong remonstrated in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The censors Chen Hou and Ji Ben and the bureau director Lin Yingcong remonstrated in succession.

sentences.zh: 帝愈怒，並下詔獄，遠謫之。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier still; all were sent to the imperial prison and exiled far away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still angrier; all were sent to the imperial prison and exiled far away.

sentences.zh: 帝必欲殺二人，變色謂閣臣蔣冕曰：「此曹誣朕不孝，罪當死。」

translations.literal: The emperor was determined to kill the two men; his countenance changed as he said to the Grand Secretariat member Jiang Mian: "These men falsely accuse Us of unfilial conduct; the crime deserves death."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was determined to kill the two men; his countenance changed as he said to the Grand Secretariat member Jiang Mian: "These men falsely accuse me of unfilial conduct; the crime deserves death."

sentences.zh: 冕膝行頓首請曰：「陛下方興堯、舜之治，奈何有殺諫臣名。」

translations.literal: Mian crawled on his knees, bowing his head, and pleaded: "Your Majesty is just now raising the governance of Yao and Shun—how can there be a name for killing remonstrating ministers?"
translations.idiomatic: Mian crawled on his knees, bowing his head, and pleaded: "Your Majesty is just now raising the governance of Yao and Shun—how can there be a name for killing remonstrating ministers?"

sentences.zh: 良久，色稍解，欲戍之。

translations.literal: After a long while his expression eased somewhat; he wished to banish them to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while his expression eased somewhat; he wished to banish them to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 冕又固請，繼以泣。

translations.literal: Mian again pressed his plea, continuing with tears.
translations.idiomatic: Mian pressed his plea again, continuing with tears.

sentences.zh: 乃杖八十，除名為民，兩人遂廢。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were beaten eighty strokes, stripped of office and made commoners; the two men were thus ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they were beaten eighty strokes, stripped of office and made commoners; the two men were thus ruined.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多論薦，不復召。

translations.literal: Many court officials recommended them; they were never summoned again.
translations.idiomatic: Many court officials recommended them, but they were never summoned again.

sentences.zh: 淛為人長者，不欺人，或為人欺亦不校。

translations.literal: Zhe as a man was magnanimous; he did not deceive others, and if others deceived him he did not contend.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe was a man of forbearance; he did not deceive others, and if others deceived him he did not contend.

sentences.zh: 與明衡皆貧，淛尤甚。

translations.literal: He and Mingheng were both poor; Zhe was especially so.
translations.idiomatic: He and Mingheng were both poor; Zhe was especially so.

sentences.zh: 鄉里利病，必與有司言，雖忤弗顧。

translations.literal: On benefits and harms to the village and district, he always spoke with the local officials, even if it offended them.
translations.idiomatic: On matters of benefit and harm to the village and district, he always spoke with the local officials, even if it offended them.

sentences.zh: 家居三十余年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for more than thirty years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for more than thirty years before he died.

sentences.zh: 明衡，字子萃。

translations.literal: Mingheng, style Zicui.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Mingheng, styled Zicui.

sentences.zh: 父思聰，死宸濠難，自有傳。

translations.literal: His father Sicong died in the Prince of Ning rebellion; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sicong died in the Prince of Ning rebellion; he has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 明衡登正德十二年進士，授太常博士。

translations.literal: Mingheng passed the jinshi in the twelfth year of Zhengde and was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Mingheng passed the jinshi in the twelfth year of Zhengde and was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 甫為御史，即與淛同得罪。

translations.literal: Barely had he become a censor when he offended together with Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Barely had he become a censor when he offended together with Zhe.

sentences.zh: 閩中學者率以蔡清為宗，至明衡獨受業於王守仁。

translations.literal: Scholars in Fujian generally took Cai Qing as their master; only Mingheng received instruction from Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars in Fujian generally took Cai Qing as their master; only Mingheng received instruction from Wang Shouren.

sentences.zh: 閩中有王氏學，自明衡始。

translations.literal: In Fujian there was Wang's learning; it began with Mingheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yangming's learning in Fujian began with Mingheng.

sentences.zh: 陳逅，字良會，常熟人。

translations.literal: Chen Hou, style Lianghui, was a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hou, styled Lianghui, came from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 除福清知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Fuqing county.

sentences.zh: 入為御史。

translations.literal: He entered [service] as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a censor.

sentences.zh: 以救兩人謫合浦主簿。

translations.literal: For saving the two men he was demoted to registrar of Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had pleaded for the two men, he was demoted to registrar at Hepu.

sentences.zh: 累官河南副使。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he rose to vice commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to vice commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 帝幸承天，坐供具不辦，下獄為民。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Chengtian, he was punished because supplies were not prepared; he was imprisoned and then made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Chengtian, he was charged with failing to prepare ceremonial supplies, imprisoned, and dismissed to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 林應驄，亦莆田人。

translations.literal: Lin Yingcong was also a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yingcong was also from Putian.

sentences.zh: 明衡同年進士。

translations.literal: He and Mingheng were jinshi of the same year.
translations.idiomatic: He and Ma Mingheng had received their jinshi degrees in the same year.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，尚書孫交核各官莊田。

translations.literal: In the early Jiajing reign, Minister Sun Jiao audited each official's manor estates.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign, Minister Sun Jiao audited the manor estates held by officials.

sentences.zh: 帝以其數稍參差，有旨詰狀。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the figures were somewhat inconsistent, issued an edict demanding explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Because the figures were somewhat inconsistent, the emperor issued an edict demanding an accounting.

sentences.zh: 應驄言：「部疏，臣司檢視，即有誤，當罪臣。

translations.literal: Yingcong said: "In the ministry memorial, I personally supervised the inspection; if there is error, I should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Yingcong said: "In the ministry memorial, I personally supervised the inspection; if there is any mistake, the blame should fall on me.

sentences.zh: 尚書總領部事，安能遍閱？

translations.literal: The minister presides over the ministry's affairs—how can he read through everything?
translations.idiomatic: The minister presides over the ministry's affairs—how could he read through everything himself?

sentences.zh: 今旬日間，戶、工二部尚書相繼令對狀，非尊賢優老之意。」

translations.literal: Within the last ten days, the ministers of Revenue and Works have been made to face inquiry in succession—this is not the intent of honoring the worthy and cherishing the aged."
translations.idiomatic: Within the past ten days the ministers of Revenue and Works have been made to face imperial inquiry in succession—this is not what it means to honor the worthy and show forbearance to the aged."

sentences.zh: 疏入，奪俸。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, his salary was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, his salary was suspended.

sentences.zh: 以救淛等，謫徐聞縣丞。

translations.literal: For saving Zhu Zhe and others, he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Xuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had pleaded for Zhu Zhe and the others, he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Xuwen.

sentences.zh: 代其長朝覲，疏陳時事，多議行。

translations.literal: Substituting for his superior at court audience, he memorialized on current affairs; most of his proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Standing in for his superior at the court audience, he memorialized on current affairs, and most of what he proposed was put into practice.

sentences.zh: 楊言，字惟仁，鄞人。

translations.literal: Yang Yan, style Weiren, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan, styled Weiren, came from Yin county.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhengde he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixteenth year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed a courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年擢禮科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Rites section.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiajing he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Rites section.

sentences.zh: 閱數日即上言：「邇者仁壽宮災，諭群臣修省。

translations.literal: Within a few days he memorialized: "Recently the Renshou Palace burned, and Your Majesty exhorted the officials to cultivate self-reflection.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days he memorialized: "Recently the Renshou Palace burned, and Your Majesty exhorted the whole court to cultivate self-reflection.

sentences.zh: 臣以為責在公卿而不在陛下，罪在諫官而不在聖躬。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the responsibility lies with the high ministers and not with Your Majesty, and the fault lies with remonstrating officials and not with the sacred person.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that the responsibility lies with the chief ministers, not with Your Majesty, and the fault lies with remonstrating officials, not with the sacred person of the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 朝廷設六科，所以舉正欺蔽也。

translations.literal: The court established the six supervising secretariats in order to expose and correct concealment and deception.
translations.idiomatic: The court established the six supervising secretariats precisely to expose concealment and set matters right.

sentences.zh: 今吏科失職，致陛下賢否混淆，進退失當。

translations.literal: Now the Personnel section has failed in its duty, causing Your Majesty to confuse worthy and unworthy and to make improper appointments and dismissals.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Personnel section has failed in its duty, so that worthy and unworthy are confused in Your Majesty's eyes and appointments and dismissals go awry.

sentences.zh: 大臣蔣冕、林俊輩去矣，小臣王相、張漢卿輩皆得禍矣，而張驄、桂萼始由捷徑以竊清秩，終怙威勢以賊良善。

translations.literal: Great ministers such as Jiang Mian and Lin Jun have departed; minor officials such as Wang Xiang and Zhang Hanqing have all suffered disaster; yet Zhang Cong and Gui E first seized clean offices by a shortcut and in the end relied on their power to injure the good.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers such as Jiang Mian and Lin Jun are gone; minor officials such as Wang Xiang and Zhang Hanqing have all come to ruin; yet Zhang Cong and Gui E first climbed by a back door into respectable rank and in the end used their power to prey on the good.

sentences.zh: 戶科失職，致陛下儉德不聞，而張侖輩請索無厭，崔和輩敢亂舊章。

translations.literal: The Revenue section has failed in its duty, so that Your Majesty's frugal virtue is not heard of, while men such as Zhang Lun demand without end and men such as Cui He dare to disturb old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue section has failed in its duty, so that Your Majesty's reputation for frugality is never heard, while men such as Zhang Lun ask without satiety and men such as Cui He dare to overturn established rules.

sentences.zh: 禮科失職，致陛下享祀未格於神，而廟社無帡幪之庇。

translations.literal: The Rites section has failed in its duty, so that Your Majesty's sacrificial offerings do not reach the spirits, and the altars of state lack sheltering protection.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites section has failed in its duty, so that Your Majesty's sacrifices do not win the spirits' assent and the altars of state lack protecting shelter.

sentences.zh: 兵科失職，致陛下綱紀廢弛，而錦衣多冒濫之官，山海攘抽分之利，匠役增收而不禁，奏帶逾額而不裁。

translations.literal: The War section has failed in its duty, so that Your Majesty's discipline is lax; the Embroidered Uniform Guard has many illicitly appointed officers; mountain and sea revenues are seized for private shares; artisan corvée levies increase without restraint; and memorial-conferred ranks exceed the quota without being trimmed.
translations.idiomatic: The War section has failed in its duty, so that discipline is slack; the Embroidered Uniform Guard is swollen with illicit appointments; revenues from mountains and seas are grabbed for private shares; artisan corvée levies rise without check; and memorial-conferred ranks exceed the quota without being cut back.

sentences.zh: 刑科失職，致陛下用罰不中。

translations.literal: The Justice section has failed in its duty, so that Your Majesty's use of punishment is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The Justice section has failed in its duty, so that punishments are not applied as they should be.

sentences.zh: 元惡如藍華輩得寬籍沒之法，諍臣如郭楠輩反施鈕械之刑。

translations.literal: Arch-villains such as Lan Hua obtain leniency under the law of confiscation, while remonstrating ministers such as Guo Nan are instead subjected to shackles.
translations.idiomatic: Arch-criminals such as Lan Hua win leniency under the law of confiscation, while remonstrating ministers such as Guo Nan are put in shackles instead.

sentences.zh: 工科失職，致陛下興作不常。

translations.literal: The Works section has failed in its duty, so that Your Majesty's construction projects are inconstant.
translations.idiomatic: The Works section has failed in its duty, so that construction projects never settle into a steady course.

sentences.zh: 局官陸宣輩支俸逾於常制，內監陳林輩抽解及於蕪湖。

translations.literal: Bureau officials such as Lu Xuan draw salaries beyond the usual rule, and inner eunuchs such as Chen Lin divert funds as far as Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau officials such as Lu Xuan draw salaries above the usual scale, and inner eunuchs such as Chen Lin divert tax silver as far as Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 凡此，皆時弊之急且大，而足以拂天意者。

translations.literal: All these are urgent and great abuses of the time, sufficient to go against Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: All of these are urgent, grave abuses of the age—enough to set Heaven's will against us.

sentences.zh: 願陛下勤修庶政，而罷臣等以警有位，庶可以格天心，弭災變。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that Your Majesty diligently cultivate the myriad affairs of government and dismiss us in order to warn those in office, so that perhaps Heaven's heart may be moved and disasters allayed."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty will diligently put the government in order and dismiss us as a warning to those who hold office, so that Heaven's heart may be won back and calamities stilled."

sentences.zh: 帝以浮謗責之。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for empty slander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for reckless slander.

sentences.zh: 奸人何淵請建世室。

translations.literal: The villain He Yuan requested the establishment of a Shishi hall.
translations.idiomatic: The schemer He Yuan petitioned to build a Shishi spirit hall.

sentences.zh: 言與廷臣爭，不聽。

translations.literal: Yan disputed it together with the court officials; [the emperor] would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan joined the court officials in opposing it, but the emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 言復抗章曰：「祖宗身有天下，大宗也，君也。

translations.literal: Yan again submitted a defiant memorial saying: "The ancestors personally possessed All-under-Heaven; they were the great lineage and they were sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: Yan again submitted a defiant memorial: "The ancestors personally possessed the realm; they were the great lineage and they were sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 獻皇帝舊為藩王，小宗也，臣也。

translations.literal: The Xian Emperor was formerly a feudal prince; he was the lesser lineage and he was a subject.
translations.idiomatic: The Xian Emperor was once a feudal prince—a lesser lineage and a subject.

sentences.zh: 以臣並君，亂天下大分。

translations.literal: To set a subject beside a sovereign confuses the great divisions of All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: To set a subject beside a sovereign overturns the great divisions of the realm.

sentences.zh: 以小宗並大宗，幹天下正統。

translations.literal: To set the lesser lineage beside the great lineage violates the legitimate succession of All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: To set the lesser lineage beside the great lineage assaults the legitimate succession of the realm.

sentences.zh: 獻帝雖有盛德，非若周文、武創王業也，欲襲世室名，舛矣。

translations.literal: Although the Xian Emperor had great virtue, he was not like King Wen and King Wu of Zhou, who founded royal enterprises; to wish to take the name Shishi is perverse.
translations.idiomatic: Although the Xian Emperor possessed great virtue, he was not like King Wen and King Wu of Zhou, who founded a royal enterprise; to claim the title Shishi is simply wrong.

sentences.zh: 如以獻帝為自出之帝，是前無祖宗；

translations.literal: If the Xian Emperor were treated as an emperor of independent origin, then there would be no ancestors before him;
translations.idiomatic: If the Xian Emperor were treated as an emperor who arose on his own, there would be no ancestors before him;

sentences.zh: 以獻帝為禰而宗之，是後無孝、武二帝。

translations.literal: if he were taken as the founder and enshrined as ancestor, then there would be no Xiaozong and Wuzong emperors after him.
translations.idiomatic: if he were taken as founder-ancestor and enshrined as such, there would be no Emperor Xiaozong or Emperor Wuzong after him.

sentences.zh: 陛下前既罪醫士劉惠之言，今乃納淵之說。

translations.literal: Your Majesty formerly punished the words of the physician Liu Hui, yet now accepts Yuan's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty formerly punished the physician Liu Hui for his words, yet now accepts He Yuan's proposal.

sentences.zh: 前既俞禮卿席書之議，今乃咈書之言。

translations.literal: Formerly Your Majesty approved the proposal of Vice Minister of Rites Xi Shu, yet now contradicts Shu's words.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Your Majesty approved Vice Minister of Rites Xi Shu's proposal, yet now you contradict what Shu said.

sentences.zh: 臣不知其何謂也。」

translations.literal: Your servant does not know what this is supposed to mean."
translations.idiomatic: I do not know what this is supposed to mean."

sentences.zh: 楊一清召入內閣，言請留之三邊。

translations.literal: Yang Yiqing was summoned into the Grand Secretariat; Yan requested that he be kept on the three frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yiqing was summoned into the Grand Secretariat, Yan asked that he be kept in charge of the three border regions.

sentences.zh: 特旨拜張璁兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: By special edict Zhang Cong was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: By special edict Zhang Cong was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 言以璁貪佞險躁，且新進，未更國家事，請罷璁，並劾吏部尚書廖紀引匪人。

translations.literal: Yan, on the grounds that Cong was greedy, fawning, dangerous, and rash, and moreover newly advanced and never having handled state affairs, requested Cong's dismissal and also impeached Minister of Personnel Liao Ji for introducing unworthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Yan argued that Cong was greedy, fawning, dangerous, and rash, that as a newcomer he had never handled state affairs, and asked that Cong be dismissed; he also impeached Minister of Personnel Liao Ji for bringing in unworthy men.

sentences.zh: 同官解一貫等亦諫。

translations.literal: His colleagues Jie Yiguan and others also remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues Jie Yiguan and others remonstrated as well.

sentences.zh: 皆不納。

translations.literal: All were rejected.
translations.idiomatic: None of it was accepted.

sentences.zh: 有投匿名書禦道者，言請即燒之，報可。

translations.literal: When an anonymous letter was cast on the Imperial Way, Yan requested that it be burned immediately; the reply was approval.
translations.idiomatic: When an anonymous letter was cast on the Imperial Way, Yan asked that it be burned at once; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 六年，錦衣百戶王邦奇借哈密事請誅楊廷和、彭澤等，下部議，未覆，而邦奇復誣大學士費宏、石缶陰庇廷和，詞連廷和子主事惇等，將興大獄。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Embroidered Uniform Guard centurion Wang Bangqi, using the Hami affair, requested the execution of Yang Tinghe, Peng Ze, and others; the matter was sent down to the ministries for discussion and had not yet been answered when Bangqi again slandered Grand Secretaries Fei Hong and Shi Gui for secretly shielding Tinghe, with words implicating Tinghe's son the director Dun and others, about to launch a great prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Embroidered Uniform Guard centurion Wang Bangqi used the Hami affair to demand the execution of Yang Tinghe, Peng Ze, and others; the case was sent to the ministries for discussion and had not yet been answered when Bangqi again accused Grand Secretaries Fei Hong and Shi Gui of secretly shielding Tinghe, implicating Tinghe's son the director Dun and others and threatening a major purge.

sentences.zh: 言抗疏曰：「先帝晏駕，江彬手握邊軍四萬，圖為不軌。

translations.literal: Yan submitted a defiant memorial saying: "When the late emperor passed away, Jiang Bin held forty thousand border troops in his grasp and plotted irregular conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yan submitted a defiant memorial: "When the late emperor passed away, Jiang Bin held forty thousand border troops in his hands and plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 廷和密謀行誅，俄頃事定，迎立聖主，此社稷之勛也。

translations.literal: Tinghe secretly plotted to carry out execution; in a moment affairs were settled and the sage sovereign was welcomed and established—this was a merit to the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe secretly planned the execution; in a moment the crisis was settled and the sage sovereign was enthroned—this was a service to the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 縱使有罪，猶當十世宥之。

translations.literal: Even if he had guilt, he should still be pardoned for ten generations.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he were guilty, he should still be pardoned for ten generations.

sentences.zh: 今既以奸人言罷其官、戍其長子矣，乃又聽邦奇之誣而盡逮其鄉里、親戚，誣為蜀黨，何意聖明之朝，忽有此事？

translations.literal: Now, on a villain's accusation, his office has already been removed and his eldest son exiled; yet again [Your Majesty] listens to Bangqi's slander and arrests all his townsfolk and kin, falsely calling them the Shu faction—what meaning can there be that in so sage and enlightened a court such a thing should suddenly arise?
translations.idiomatic: Already, on a villain's accusation, his office has been taken away and his eldest son exiled; yet now Your Majesty again listens to Bangqi's slander and arrests all his townsfolk and kin, falsely branding them the Shu faction—what can it mean that in so enlightened a court such a thing should suddenly appear?

sentences.zh: 至宏、缶乃天子師保之官，百僚之表也。

translations.literal: As for Hong and Gui, they are the emperor's tutors and guardians, the model for the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: As for Fei Hong and Shi Gui, they are the emperor's tutors and guardians—the model for the whole bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 邦奇心懷怨望，文飾奸言，詬辱大臣，熒惑聖聽。

translations.literal: Bangqi harbors resentment, adorns wicked words, reviles great ministers, and deludes the sacred hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Bangqi harbors resentment, dresses up wicked words, reviles great ministers, and misleads the sacred ear.

sentences.zh: 若窮治不已，株連益多，臣竊為國家大體惜也。」

translations.literal: If prosecution is pushed to the end without cease, implicated persons will grow ever more numerous; your servant privately grieves for the great body of the state."
translations.idiomatic: If the investigation is driven to the bitter end, ever more people will be dragged in; I grieve privately for the fundamental interests of the state."

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝震怒，並收系言，親鞫於午門。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was greatly enraged; Yan was seized and interrogated in person at the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was furious; Yan was seized and the emperor personally interrogated him at the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 群臣悉集。

translations.literal: All the officials assembled.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court assembled to witness it.

sentences.zh: 言備極五毒，折其一指，卒無撓詞。

translations.literal: Yan was subjected to the extremes of the five punishments; one finger was broken, yet in the end he had no words of yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was tortured with every extremity of the five punishments; one finger was broken, yet in the end he would not yield a word.

sentences.zh: 既罷，下五府九卿議。

translations.literal: When it was over, the matter was sent down to the Five Offices and Nine Ministries for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When it was over, the case was sent to the Five Offices and Nine Ministries for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 鎮遠侯顧仕隆等覆奏邦奇言皆虛妄，帝責仕隆等徇情。

translations.literal: Marquis of Zhenyuan Gu Shilong and others memorialized in reply that Bangqi's words were all false; the emperor rebuked Shilong and the others for favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Zhenyuan Gu Shilong and others reported back that Bangqi's charges were all false; the emperor rebuked Shilong and the others for showing favoritism.

sentences.zh: 然獄亦因是解，謫言宿州判官。

translations.literal: Yet the prosecution was also thereby dissolved; Yan was demoted to judge of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the case was also dissolved on that account, and Yan was demoted to judge of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史程啟充請還言舊任，不聽。

translations.literal: The censor Cheng Qichong requested that Yan be restored to his former post; [the emperor] would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Cheng Qichong asked that Yan be restored to his former post, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 稍遷溧陽知縣，歷南京吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to magistrate of Liyang and served through as director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made magistrate of Liyang and rose to director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 坐事再謫知夷陵。

translations.literal: Because of an affair he was again demoted to magistrate of Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: After an offense he was demoted again to magistrate of Yiling.

sentences.zh: 累官湖廣參議。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he rose to administration commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to administration commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 言為吏，多著聲績。

translations.literal: In office Yan achieved much reputation and record.
translations.idiomatic: As an administrator Yan won a strong reputation for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 溧陽、夷陵皆祠祀之。

translations.literal: Both Liyang and Yiling enshrined him in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Both Liyang and Yiling erected shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 劉安，字汝勉，慈溪人。

translations.literal: Liu An, style Rumin, was a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu An, styled Rumin, came from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授南京工部主事，改河南道御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works and transferred to censor of the Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works, then transferred to censor of the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 入臺甫一月，上疏曰：「人君貴明不貴察。

translations.literal: Having entered the Censorate for only one month, he submitted a memorial saying: "For a ruler, clarity is prized and not keen scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month after entering the Censorate, he memorialized: "A ruler should prize clarity, not keen scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 察，非明也。

translations.literal: Scrutiny is not clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Scrutiny is not clarity.

sentences.zh: 人君以察為明，天下始多事矣。

translations.literal: When a ruler takes scrutiny for clarity, All-under-Heaven begins to have many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler mistakes scrutiny for clarity, the realm soon fills with trouble.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨禦八年而治理未臻，識者謂陛下之治功損於明察。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has faced the throne for eight years yet good governance has not been attained; those who understand say that Your Majesty's achievements in rule are diminished by keen scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned for eight years, yet good governance has not been achieved; informed observers say that your accomplishments in rule are being undermined by excessive scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 夫治，可以緩圖，不可以急取；

translations.literal: Governance can be pursued with gradual planning; it cannot be seized in haste;
translations.idiomatic: Good government can be pursued with patience; it cannot be seized in haste;

sentences.zh: 可以休養致，不可以督責成。

translations.literal: it can be brought about through nurturing rest; it cannot be completed through pressing blame.
translations.idiomatic: it can be brought about through nurturing and ease, not completed through relentless pressure and blame.

sentences.zh: 以急切之心，行督責之政，於是躬親有司之事，指摘臣下之失，令出而復返，方信而忽疑。

translations.literal: With an urgent heart, carrying out a policy of pressing blame, thereupon personally handling the affairs of the functionaries, picking out the faults of subordinates, orders issued and then reversed, just trusted and suddenly doubted.
translations.idiomatic: With an impatient heart you pursue a policy of relentless blame; then you personally take up the business of the functionaries, pick at your ministers' faults, issue orders only to reverse them, trust one moment and doubt the next.

sentences.zh: 大小臣工救過不暇，多有不安其位者。

translations.literal: Great and small officials have no leisure beyond remedying faults; many are not secure in their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Officials high and low have no time but to cover their mistakes, and many can no longer feel secure in their posts.

sentences.zh: 孰能為陛下建長久之策，以圖平治哉？

translations.literal: Who can for Your Majesty establish a long-term policy in order to seek peaceful governance?
translations.idiomatic: Who can lay before Your Majesty a long-term policy aimed at lasting peace and order?

sentences.zh: 且朝廷者，四方之極也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the court is the pole for the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the court is the pole star for the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 內之君臣，習尚如此，則外而撫按守令之官，風從響應。

translations.literal: If within, among ruler and ministers, custom and practice are thus, then without, among the grand coordinators, surveillance commissioners, and prefectural and county magistrates, wind follows and echo answers.
translations.idiomatic: If ruler and ministers at court fall into such habits, then outside, among grand coordinators, surveillance commissioners, and local magistrates, the wind will be followed and the echo will answer.

sentences.zh: 上以苛察繩，下以苛察應，恐民窮為起盜之源，食寡無強兵之理。

translations.literal: Above, using harsh scrutiny as the cord; below, responding with harsh scrutiny—I fear that when the people are impoverished it becomes the source of rising banditry, and when food is scarce there is no principle of a strong army.
translations.idiomatic: Above you bind officials with harsh scrutiny; below they answer with harsh scrutiny in turn—I fear that when the people are driven to destitution banditry will rise, and when food is scarce there can be no strong army.

sentences.zh: 今明天子綜核於上，百執事振刷於下，叢蠹之弊十去其九，所少者元氣耳。

translations.literal: Now the enlightened Son of Heaven comprehensively audits above and the hundred functionaries are shaken and polished below; the abuses of swarming corruption are nine-tenths gone—what is lacking is only vital energy.
translations.idiomatic: Today the enlightened Son of Heaven audits comprehensively above and the hundred functionaries are shaken into diligence below; the abuses of entrenched corruption are nine-tenths gone—what is lacking now is only the realm's vital energy.

sentences.zh: 伏望大包荒之量，重根本之圖，略繁文而先急務，簡細故而弘遠猷，不以一人之毀譽為喜怒，不以一言之順逆為行止，久任老成，優容言官，則君臣上下一德一心，人人各安其位，事事各盡其才，雍熙太和之治不難見矣。」

translations.literal: Your servant humbly hopes for the magnanimity of great tolerance for negligence, to weight the fundamental plan, to set aside verbose documents and put urgent affairs first, to simplify minor matters and enlarge far-reaching designs, not to make joy or anger from one man's praise or blame, not to make action or stopping from one statement's accord or opposition, to employ the aged and experienced for long tenure, to show forbearance to remonstrating officials—then ruler and ministers above and below will be of one virtue and one heart, each man secure in his post, each affair fully using its talent, and the governance of radiant harmony and great peace will not be hard to see."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will embrace the magnanimity that tolerates much negligence, give weight to fundamental plans, set aside verbose paperwork and put urgent affairs first, simplify petty matters and enlarge far-reaching designs, neither rejoice nor rage at one man's praise or blame, neither advance nor halt on the strength of a single remark, keep the aged and experienced in office for long tenures, and show forbearance to remonstrating officials—then ruler and ministers will be of one mind, each man secure in his post and each task fulfilled by its proper talent, and a reign of radiant harmony will not be far to seek."

sentences.zh: 帝閱疏大怒，逮赴錦衣衛拷訊。

translations.literal: When the emperor read the memorial he was greatly enraged; [An] was seized and sent to the Embroidered Uniform Guard for torture and interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read the memorial he was furious; An was seized and sent to the Embroidered Uniform Guard for torture and interrogation.

sentences.zh: 兵科給事中胡堯時救之，並逮治。

translations.literal: The War-section supervising secretary Hu Yaoshi pleaded for him and was also seized for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The War-section supervising secretary Hu Yaoshi pleaded for him and was seized and punished as well.

sentences.zh: 獄具，謫堯時攸縣主薄，安餘於典史。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, Yaoshi was demoted to registrar of You county and An to county recorder of Yuyu.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was concluded, Yaoshi was demoted to registrar of You county and An to county recorder of Yuyu.

sentences.zh: 築決堤數十丈，人稱劉公堤。

translations.literal: He built up a breached dike for several dozen zhang; people called it Magistrate Liu's Dike.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired a breached dike for several dozen zhang; people called it Magistrate Liu's Dike.

sentences.zh: 再遷長沙同知，擢鳳陽知府。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to vice prefect of Changsha and promoted to prefect of Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made vice prefect of Changsha and promoted to prefect of Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 治行卓異，賜正三品服。

translations.literal: His governance and conduct were outstandingly unusual; he was granted dress of the regular third rank.
translations.idiomatic: His record in office was outstanding, and he was granted dress of the regular third rank.

sentences.zh: 以憂歸，卒。

translations.literal: He returned home on mourning leave and died.
translations.idiomatic: He went home on mourning leave and died there.

sentences.zh: 薛侃，字尚謙，揭陽人。

translations.literal: Xue Kan, style Shangqian, was a native of Jieyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Kan, styled Shangqian, came from Jieyang.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，正德十二年成進士，即以侍養歸。

translations.literal: By nature he was utmost in filial piety; in the twelfth year of Zhengde he became a jinshi and immediately returned home to attend [his parents].
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was profoundly filial; he passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Zhengde and at once returned home to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 師王守仁於贛州，歸語兄助教俊。

translations.literal: He took Wang Shouren as his teacher at Ganzhou; on returning home he told his elder brother Jun, an assistant instructor.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Wang Shouren at Ganzhou, and when he came home he told his elder brother Jun, who served as an assistant instructor.

sentences.zh: 俊大喜，率群子侄宗鎧等往學焉。

translations.literal: Jun was greatly delighted, and leading his sons, nephews, Zong Kai, and the rest, went to study there.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was overjoyed and, leading his sons and nephews including Zong Kai, went to study with him.

sentences.zh: 自是王氏學盛行於嶺南。

translations.literal: From this time the learning of the Wang school flourished widely in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Wang Yangming's teaching spread widely throughout Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，侃授行人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Kan was appointed Messenger.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Kan was appointed a Messenger in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 母訃，隕絕，五日始食粥。

translations.literal: When his mother's death notice arrived, he collapsed unconscious; only on the fifth day did he begin to eat gruel.
translations.idiomatic: When news of his mother's death arrived, he fainted outright and did not take even gruel until the fifth day.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年起故官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing he resumed his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiajing he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 聞守仁卒，偕歐陽德輩為位，朝夕哭。

translations.literal: On hearing that Shouren had died, together with Ouyang De and others he set up a mourning place and wept morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Wang Shouren had died, he and Ouyang De and others set up a mourning shrine and wept there morning and night.

sentences.zh: 時方議文廟祀典，侃請祀陸九淵、陳獻章。

translations.literal: At the time the Confucian temple sacrifices were under discussion; Kan requested sacrifices to Lu Jiuyuan and Chen Xianzhang.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was debating sacrifices in the Confucian temple, Kan petitioned that Lu Jiuyuan and Chen Xianzhang be enshrined.

sentences.zh: 九淵得報允。

translations.literal: Jiuyuan received word of approval.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jiuyuan's enshrinement was approved.

sentences.zh: 已，進司正。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was promoted to Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted to Director of Ceremonies in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 十年秋疏言：「祖宗分封子弟，必留一人京師司香，有事居守，或代行祭饗。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the tenth year he memorialized, saying: "When the founding ancestors enfeoffed their sons and younger brothers, they always left one person in the capital to tend the incense, to remain on guard when needed, or to perform sacrifices in another's stead.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the tenth year he submitted a memorial saying: "When our founding ancestors enfeoffed imperial clansmen, they always kept one kinsman in the capital to tend the ancestral incense, to hold the capital in reserve when required, or to perform the sacrifices in another's place.

sentences.zh: 列聖相承，莫之或改。

translations.literal: The successive sage emperors handed this down, and none altered it.
translations.idiomatic: Successive emperors carried on this practice without change.

sentences.zh: 至正德初，逆瑾懷貳，始令就封。

translations.literal: Down to the beginning of Zhengde, when the traitor Liu Jin harbored disloyal intent, they were first ordered to go to their fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Not until early in the Zhengde reign, when the rebel Liu Jin turned disloyal, were princes first ordered to take up residence in their fiefs.

sentences.zh: 乞稽舊典，擇親藩賢者居京師，慎選正人輔導，以待他日皇嗣之生，此宗社大計。」

translations.literal: I beg that the old statutes be consulted, that a worthy member of the close princely houses be chosen to dwell in the capital, and that upright men be carefully selected to instruct him, to await the birth of an imperial heir in days to come—this is a great plan for altar and state.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consult the ancient precedents, choose a worthy prince of the close collateral line to remain in the capital, and carefully appoint upright tutors to guide him, so that when an imperial heir is born in due time the dynasty may be secure—this is a matter vital to the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝方祈嗣，諱言之，震怒，立下獄廷鞫，究交通主使者。

translations.literal: The emperor was then praying for an heir and regarded such talk as taboo; in a thunderous rage he had Kan imprisoned at once and interrogated at court, investigating who had communicated with and instigated him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then praying for an heir and took such talk as forbidden; he flew into a rage, had Kan thrown into prison at once, and interrogated him at court to discover who had conspired with and instigated him.

sentences.zh: 南海彭澤為吏部郎，無行。

translations.literal: Peng Ze of Nanhai served as a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel and was without proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze of Nanhai was a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel and was a man of no character.

sentences.zh: 因議禮附張孚敬，遂與為腹心。

translations.literal: Because in the Rites Controversy he attached himself to Zhang Cong, he thereby became his intimate confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Having sided with Zhang Cong in the Rites Controversy, he became Zhang's trusted inner circle.

sentences.zh: 後京察被黜，孚敬奏留之，復引為諭德，至太常卿。

translations.literal: Later, in the capital evaluation he was dismissed; Zhang Cong memorialized to retain him, again drew him in as Preceptor, and he rose to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed in the metropolitan personnel review, but Zhang Cong memorialized to keep him at court, brought him back as a preceptor, and eventually had him promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 侃以疏草示澤。

translations.literal: Kan showed the draft of his memorial to Peng Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Kan showed Peng Ze the draft of his memorial.

sentences.zh: 澤與侃及少詹事夏言同年生，而言是時數忤孚敬。

translations.literal: Peng Ze, Kan, and the Junior Mentor Xia Yan had been born in the same examination year, and at this time Yan repeatedly offended Zhang Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze, Kan, and the Junior Mentor Xia Yan had passed the examinations in the same year, and at this time Xia Yan had repeatedly crossed Zhang Cong.

sentences.zh: 澤默計儲副事觸帝諱，必興大獄，誣言同謀可禍也，紿侃槁示孚敬，因報侃曰：「張公甚稱善，此國家大事，當從中贊之。」

translations.literal: Peng Ze silently calculated that the matter of the heir-presumptive touched the emperor's taboo and would surely bring a great case; falsely implicating Yan as a co-conspirator could bring disaster upon him. He deceived Kan by showing the draft to Zhang Cong, then reported to Kan: "Master Zhang greatly praised it; this is a great matter of state and should be supported from within."
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze reckoned silently that talk of the heir touched the emperor's sore point and would surely provoke a major prosecution; if he could falsely implicate Xia Yan as a co-conspirator, Yan could be ruined. He tricked Kan by showing the draft to Zhang Cong, then told Kan, "Master Zhang praised it highly. This is a matter of national importance and ought to be backed from within the court.

sentences.zh: 與為期，趣之上。

translations.literal: They fixed a date and urged him to submit it.
translations.idiomatic: They set a date and pressed him to submit the memorial.

sentences.zh: 孚敬乃先錄侃槁以進，謂出於言，請勿先發以待疏至。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong then first copied Kan's draft and submitted it, saying it had come from Xia Yan, and asked that it not be released first but that they wait until the memorial arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong then copied Kan's draft and submitted it first, claiming it had come from Xia Yan, and asked that the matter not be made public until Kan's memorial arrived.

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 侃猶豫，澤頻趣之乃上。

translations.literal: Kan hesitated; only after Peng Ze repeatedly urged him did he submit it.
translations.idiomatic: Kan hesitated, and only after Peng Ze pressed him again and again did he submit the memorial.

sentences.zh: 拷掠備至，侃獨自承，累日獄不具。

translations.literal: Torture was applied to the full; Kan alone confessed, yet for many days the case could not be completed.
translations.idiomatic: He was tortured to the utmost, yet Kan confessed alone; for many days the investigators could not close the case.

sentences.zh: 澤挑使引言，侃瞋目曰：「疏，我自具。

translations.literal: Peng Ze goaded him to implicate Yan; Kan glared and said: "The memorial—I drafted it myself.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze goaded him to implicate Xia Yan. Kan glared and said, "I wrote the memorial myself.

sentences.zh: 趣我上者，爾也。

translations.literal: The one who urged me to submit it was you.
translations.idiomatic: You were the one who pressed me to submit it.

sentences.zh: 爾謂張少傅許助之，言何豫？」

translations.literal: You said Vice Grand Tutor Zhang promised to help—what has Yan to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: You told me Vice Grand Tutor Zhang would help—what does Xia Yan have to do with any of this?

sentences.zh: 給事中孫應奎、曹汴揖孚敬避。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Sun Yingkui and Cao Bian bowed to Zhang Cong and stepped aside.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries Sun Yingkui and Cao Bian bowed to Zhang Cong and withdrew to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 孚敬怒。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong was furious.

sentences.zh: 應奎等疏聞，詔並下言、應奎、汴詔獄，命郭勛、翟鑾及司禮中官會廷臣再鞫，具得其實。

translations.literal: Yingkui and the others memorialized to inform the throne; an edict ordered Yan, Yingkui, and Bian all sent to the imperial prison, and Guo Xun, Zhai Luan, and eunuchs of the Directorate of Ceremonies were commanded to join the court officials in re-interrogating them, fully obtaining the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Yingkui and the others reported the matter in a memorial; an edict sent Xia Yan, Yingkui, and Bian together to the imperial prison and ordered Guo Xun, Zhai Luan, and eunuchs of the Directorate of Ceremonies to join the court officials in a fresh interrogation, by which the whole truth came out.

sentences.zh: 帝乃釋言等，出孚敬密疏二示廷臣，斥其忮罔，令致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor then released Yan and the others, produced two of Zhang Cong's secret memorials to show the court officials, rebuked his jealousy and deceit, and ordered him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then released Xia Yan and the others, produced two of Zhang Cong's secret memorials for the court officials to see, denounced his jealousy and deceit, and ordered him to retire.

sentences.zh: 侃為民，澤戍大同。

translations.literal: Kan was reduced to commoner status; Peng Ze was banished to garrison duty at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was stripped of office and reduced to commoner status; Peng Ze was exiled to military service at Datong.

sentences.zh: 澤在朝專為邪媚，及敗，天下快之。

translations.literal: Peng Ze in court devoted himself wholly to wicked flattery; when he fell, all under Heaven rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: In court Peng Ze had devoted himself to wicked flattery; when he fell, the empire rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 侃至潞河，遇聖壽節，焚香叩祝甚謹。

translations.literal: When Kan reached the Lu River, he encountered the emperor's birthday and, burning incense, kowtowed in prayer with great reverence.
translations.idiomatic: When Kan reached the Lu River, it happened to be the emperor's birthday; he burned incense and kowtowed in prayer with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 或報參政項喬曰：「小舟中有民服而祝聖者。」

translations.literal: Someone reported to Administration Commissioner Xiang Qiao: "In a small boat there is one in commoner's dress praying for the sage emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported to Administration Commissioner Xiang Qiao, "There is a man in commoner's dress aboard a small boat praying for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 喬曰：「必薛中離也。」

translations.literal: Qiao said: "It must be Xue Zhongli."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Qiao said, "That must be Zhongli."

sentences.zh: 跡之，果然。

translations.literal: They tracked him, and so it was.
translations.idiomatic: They tracked him down, and so it proved.

sentences.zh: 中離者，侃自號也。

translations.literal: Zhongli was Kan's sobriquet for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli was the sobriquet Kan had taken for himself.

sentences.zh: 歸家益力學，從遊者百余人。

translations.literal: Returning home he applied himself all the more to learning, and those who followed him in study numbered more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he threw himself all the more into scholarship, and more than a hundred students came to study with him.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復官，贈御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing his office was restored, and he was posthumously given the title Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign his office was restored and he was posthumously enfeoffed as a censor.

sentences.zh: 俊子宗鎧，自有傳。

translations.literal: Jun's son Zong Kai has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's son Zong Kai has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 侃歸數月，御史喻希禮、石金皆以言皇嗣得罪。

translations.literal: Several months after Kan returned home, the censors Yu Xili and Shi Jin both offended by speaking of the imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: A few months after Kan returned home, the censors Yu Xili and Shi Jin were both punished for speaking about the imperial heir.

sentences.zh: 希禮言：「陛下祈嗣禮成，瑞雪遂降，臣以為招和致祥，不盡於此。

translations.literal: Xili said: "Your Majesty's rites praying for an heir have been completed, and auspicious snow has thereupon fallen; your servant considers that summoning harmony and bringing felicity is not exhausted in this alone.
translations.idiomatic: Xili wrote, "Your Majesty's rites praying for an heir have been completed and auspicious snow has fallen; I believe that summoning harmony and securing blessings need not stop here.

sentences.zh: 往者大赦，今歲免刑，臣民盡沾澤，獨議禮議獄得罪諸臣遠戍邊僥，乞量移近地，或特賜赦免，則和氣薰蒸，前星自耀。」

translations.literal: Formerly there was a great amnesty; this year punishments were remitted—the ministers and people all received grace—yet alone the various officials condemned in the Rites Controversy and its prosecutions remain banished far to the border marches. I beg that they be moved by degrees to nearer places, or specially granted pardon and release; then harmonious qi will suffuse and the heir-star will shine of itself."
translations.idiomatic: There has been a great amnesty in the past and punishments were remitted this year—the ministers and people have all shared in imperial grace—yet the officials condemned in the Rites Controversy and its prosecutions alone remain exiled to distant border posts. I beg that they be transferred by degrees to nearer places, or specially pardoned and released; then harmonious qi will suffuse the realm and the heir-star will shine of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒曰：「謂朕罪諸臣致遲嗣續耶？

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and said: "Do you mean that I punished these officials and thereby delayed the succession?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and said, "Are you saying that I punished those officials and thereby delayed the birth of an heir?

sentences.zh: 所司參議以聞。」

translations.literal: Let the responsible offices deliberate and report."
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible offices deliberate and report."

sentences.zh: 議未上，金亦言：「陛下一日萬幾，經理勞瘁。

translations.literal: Before the deliberation was submitted, Jin also said: "Your Majesty handles ten thousand affairs in a day and is worn out in managing them.
translations.idiomatic: Before the deliberation was submitted, Shi Jin also wrote, "Your Majesty handles ten thousand affairs in a day and is worn out with managing them.

sentences.zh: 何若中涵太虛，物來順應。

translations.literal: How much better to hold the Great Void within and let things come and respond in accord.
translations.idiomatic: How much better to hold the Great Void within and let things come and be met as they arrive.

sentences.zh: 凡人才之用舍，政事之敷施，始以九卿之詳度，繼以內閣之咨謀，其弗協於中者，付諸臺諫之公論。

translations.literal: As for the employment or dismissal of men of talent and the carrying out of government affairs, let them first be thoroughly weighed by the Nine Ministers, next be consulted upon by the Grand Secretariat; what does not accord with the mean should be entrusted to the remonstrance and censorate bureaus' public judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Let the appointment or dismissal of talent and the conduct of government affairs first be weighed in detail by the Nine Ministers, then discussed in the Grand Secretariat; whatever still fails to accord with the mean should be left to the censorate's public judgment.

sentences.zh: 陛下恭默凝神，挈其綱領，使精神內蘊，根本充固，則百斯男之慶，自不期而至。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, reverently silent and concentrating your spirit, should grasp the guiding principles, let spirit be stored within and the root made full and firm—then the blessing of countless sons will arrive unbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, reverently silent and concentrating your spirit, should grasp the guiding principles, let your inner spirit be stored up and your foundation made firm—then the blessing of countless sons will come without your seeking it.

sentences.zh: 王守仁首平逆藩，繼靖巨寇，乃因疑謗，泯其前勞。

translations.literal: Wang Shouren first pacified the rebellious princedom, then quelled great bandits—yet because of suspicion and slander his earlier merit was effaced.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren first pacified the rebellious princedom and then quelled great bandits, yet because of suspicion and slander his earlier achievements were erased.

sentences.zh: 大禮大獄諸臣，久膺流竄，因郁既久，物故已多。

translations.literal: The various officials of the Great Rites and the great prosecutions have long suffered exile; oppressed for so long, many have already died.
translations.idiomatic: The officials condemned in the Great Rites and the great prosecutions have long been in exile; crushed by grief for so long, many have already died.

sentences.zh: 望錄守仁功，寬諸臣罪，則太和之氣塞宇宙間矣。」

translations.literal: I hope that Shouren's merit may be recorded and the crimes of the various officials pardoned; then the qi of supreme harmony will fill the space between heaven and earth."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Wang Shouren's achievements be recorded and those officials' crimes pardoned; then the qi of supreme harmony will fill the universe.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅曰：「金欲朕勿禦萬幾，即古奸臣導其君不親政之意，其並察奏。」

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and said: "Jin wants me not to attend to the myriad affairs—this is the meaning by which ancient treacherous ministers led their rulers not to govern in person; let both be investigated and reported."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and said, "Shi Jin wants me to leave the myriad affairs of state unattended—this is exactly how treacherous ministers of old led their rulers to neglect government in person. Investigate and report on them both."

sentences.zh: 尚書夏言等言二人無他腸。

translations.literal: The Minister Xia Yan and others said the two men had no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister Xia Yan and others said the two men had no ulterior motive.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，下二人詔獄，而責言等陳狀。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier, sent the two men to the imperial prison, and rebuked Yan and the others to state the facts clearly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still angrier, sent the two men to the imperial prison, and rebuked Xia Yan and the others to set out the facts clearly.

sentences.zh: 伏罪乃宥之。

translations.literal: Only after they confessed guilt were they pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Only after they confessed guilt were they spared.

sentences.zh: 二人竟謫戍邊衛。

translations.literal: The two men in the end were demoted and banished to border garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the two men were demoted and exiled to border garrisons.

sentences.zh: 久之，赦還，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time they were pardoned and returned; they died.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward they were pardoned and allowed to return; both died in the end.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，俱贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing both were posthumously given the title Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign both were posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Ministers of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 喻希禮，麻城人。

translations.literal: Yu Xili was a native of Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xili came from Macheng.

sentences.zh: 石金，黃梅人。

translations.literal: Shi Jin was a native of Huangmei.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jin came from Huangmei.

sentences.zh: 巡按廣西，與姚鏌不協。

translations.literal: While touring and inspecting Guangxi, he was at odds with Yao Nai.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as touring inspector of Guangxi, he fell out with Yao Nai.

sentences.zh: 後與守仁共撫盧蘇、王受。

translations.literal: Later, together with Shouren, he jointly pacified Lu Su and Wang Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Wang Shouren in pacifying Lu Su and Wang Shou.

sentences.zh: 還臺，值張、桂用事。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital censorate, it happened that Zhang and Gui held power.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital censorate, Zhang Cong and Gui E were in power.

sentences.zh: 御史儲良才輩爭附之，金獨侃侃不阿，以是有名。

translations.literal: The censors Chu Liangcai and others vied to attach themselves to them; Jin alone was forthright and would not yield, and thereby gained a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Censors such as Chu Liangcai vied to attach themselves to the faction, but Jin alone stood forthright and unbending, and thereby won renown.

sentences.zh: 楊名，字實卿，遂寧人。

translations.literal: Yang Ming, style Shiqing, was a native of Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ming, styled Shiqing, came from Suining.

sentences.zh: 童子時，督學王廷相奇其語，補弟子員。

translations.literal: As a boy, Education Intendant Wang Tingxiang marveled at his speech and enrolled him as a student member.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, Education Intendant Wang Tingxiang was struck by his eloquence and enrolled him as a licentiate student.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年，鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing he placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiajing he took first place in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 明年以第三人及第，授編修。

translations.literal: The next year he passed the palace examination in third place and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he passed the palace examination in third place and was appointed a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 聞大母喪，請急歸。

translations.literal: On hearing of his great-grandmother's death, he requested urgent leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of his great-grandmother's death, he requested emergency leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 還朝，為展書官。

translations.literal: On returning to court he served as book-presenting officer.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court he served as a book-presenting officer.

sentences.zh: 十一年十月，彗星見。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eleventh year a comet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eleventh year a comet appeared.

sentences.zh: 名應詔上書，言帝喜怒失中，用舍不當。

translations.literal: Ming responded to the edict with a memorial, saying the emperor's joy and anger had lost the mean and his employment and dismissal were improper.
translations.idiomatic: Ming responded to the imperial edict with a memorial saying the emperor's joy and anger had lost their balance and his appointments and dismissals were improper.
