sentences.zh: 語切直，帝銜之，而答旨稱其納忠，令無隱。

translations.literal: His language was cutting and direct; the emperor harbored resentment, yet in the reply edict praised his offering loyalty and ordered him to conceal nothing.
translations.idiomatic: His language was blunt and direct; the emperor nursed a grudge, yet in his reply praised Ming for offering loyal counsel and told him to hold nothing back.

sentences.zh: 名乃復言：「吏部諸曹之首，尚書百官之表，而汪鋐小人之尤也。

translations.literal: Ming then spoke again: "Of all the bureaus of the Ministry of Personnel the first is foremost, and the Minister is the model for the hundred officials—yet Wang Jixiang is the worst of petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Ming then wrote again: "The Ministry of Personnel heads all the ministries, and its minister is the model for the hundred officials—yet Wang Jixiang is the worst sort of petty man.

sentences.zh: 武定侯郭勛奸回險譎，太常卿陳道瀛、金赟仁粗鄙酣淫。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun is treacherous, crooked, and deceitful; the Minister of Ceremonies Chen Daoyuan and Jin Yunren are coarse, vulgar, and drunkenly dissolute.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun is treacherous, crooked, and deceitful; the Minister of Ceremonies Chen Daoyuan and Jin Yunren are coarse, vulgar, and drunkenly dissolute.

sentences.zh: 數人者，群情皆曰不當用，而陛下用之，是聖心之偏於喜也。

translations.literal: These several men—all public sentiment says they ought not be employed, yet Your Majesty employs them; this is the sage heart's bias toward what pleases it.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion holds that none of these men ought to be employed, yet Your Majesty employs them—this shows that the imperial mind is biased toward what pleases it.

sentences.zh: 諸臣建言觸忤者，心實可原。

translations.literal: The various officials whose remonstrances gave offense—their hearts may truly be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: The officials whose remonstrances gave offense are in truth deserving of forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 大學士李時以愛惜人才為請，即荷嘉納，而吏部不為題覆。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Shi pleaded to cherish men of talent and at once received gracious acceptance—yet the Ministry of Personnel did not draft a reply.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Shi pleaded to cherish talent and was graciously accepted at once—yet the Ministry of Personnel never drafted a formal reply.

sentences.zh: 臣所謂虛文塞責者，豈盡無哉？

translations.literal: What your servant calls empty documents that block responsibility—is there truly none of this?
translations.idiomatic: Are there truly none of the empty formalities I speak of that merely shift responsibility?

sentences.zh: 夫此得罪諸臣，群情以為當宥，而陛下不終宥，是聖心之偏於怒也。

translations.literal: As for these offending officials, public sentiment holds they ought to be pardoned, yet Your Majesty does not pardon them to the end—this is the sage heart's bias toward anger.
translations.idiomatic: As for these punished officials, public opinion holds they ought to be pardoned, yet Your Majesty will not pardon them in the end—this shows that the imperial mind is biased toward anger.

sentences.zh: 真人邵元節猥以末術，過蒙采聽。

translations.literal: The Perfected Man Shao Yuanjie, with base minor arts, has excessively received Your Majesty's attention and acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: The Perfected Man Shao Yuanjie, with his petty arts, has been far too much heeded by Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 嘗令設醮內府，且命左右大臣奔走供事，遂致不肖之徒有昏夜乞哀出其門者。

translations.literal: He was once ordered to set up a ritual altar in the inner palace, and senior ministers at the emperor's side were commanded to run about supplying the service, so that unworthy men came to beg for mercy at his gate in the dark of night.
translations.idiomatic: He was once ordered to perform a ritual in the inner palace, and senior ministers were made to run about serving him, so that unworthy men came to beg for favor at his gate in the dead of night.

sentences.zh: 書之史冊，後世其將謂何？

translations.literal: When this is written in the historical records, what will later ages say?
translations.idiomatic: When this is written in the historical records, what will posterity say?

sentences.zh: 凡此聖心之少有所偏者，故臣敢抒其狂愚。」

translations.literal: In all these matters the sage heart has been somewhat biased; therefore your servant dares express his reckless folly."
translations.idiomatic: In all these matters the imperial mind has been somewhat biased; therefore I dare speak my reckless folly.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝震怒，即執下詔獄拷訊。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was shaken with rage and at once had him seized and sent to the imperial prison for interrogation under torture.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was shaken with rage and at once had Ming seized and sent to the imperial prison for interrogation under torture.

sentences.zh: 鋐疏辨，謂：「名乃楊廷和鄉人。

translations.literal: Wang Jixiang memorialized in his own defense, saying: "Ming is a fellow townsman of Yang Tinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jixiang memorialized in his own defense, saying, "Ming is a fellow townsman of Yang Tinghe.

sentences.zh: 頃張孚敬去位，廷和黨輒思報復，故攻及臣。

translations.literal: Just now Zhang Cong left office, and the Yang Tinghe faction at once thought of revenge; therefore they attacked down to me.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Zhang Cong has left office, Yang Tinghe's faction at once seeks revenge, and so their attack has reached me.

sentences.zh: 臣為上簡用，誠欲一振舉朝廷之法，而議者輒病臣操切。

translations.literal: Your servant was selected and employed by Your Majesty and truly wished to revive the laws of the court in one effort, yet those who discuss affairs constantly fault your servant for being harsh and pressing.
translations.idiomatic: I was selected and employed by Your Majesty and truly wished to revive the laws of the court at a stroke, yet critics constantly fault me for being harsh and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 且內閣大臣率務和同，植黨固位，故名敢欺肆至此。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the Grand Secretariat ministers as a rule pursue harmony and agreement, plant factions and secure their posts—therefore Ming dares to insult and act wildly to this extent."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, grand secretaries as a rule pursue harmony, build factions, and secure their posts—therefore Ming dares to insult and act wildly to this extent.

sentences.zh: 帝深入其言，益怒，命所司窮詰主使。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply swayed by his words, grew still angrier, and ordered the responsible offices to investigate thoroughly who had instigated it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply swayed by his words, grew still angrier, and ordered the responsible offices to investigate thoroughly who had instigated the attack.

sentences.zh: 名數瀕於死，無所承，言曾以疏草示同年生程文德，乃並文德下獄。

translations.literal: Ming several times neared death and confessed to nothing; he said he had once shown the draft memorial to his examination-year fellow Cheng Wende, and so Wende too was sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Ming was tortured nearly to death but confessed to nothing; he said he had once shown the draft to his examination-year fellow Cheng Wende, and so Wende too was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 侍郎黃宗明、候補判官黃直救之，先後皆下獄。

translations.literal: The Vice Minister Huang Zongming and the candidate judge Huang Zhi came to his rescue; both in turn were sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Huang Zongming and candidate judge Huang Zhi came to his rescue; both were thrown into prison in turn.

sentences.zh: 法司再擬名罪，皆不當上指。

translations.literal: The judicial offices twice drafted Ming's crime, yet neither accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices twice drafted sentences for Ming, yet neither satisfied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 特詔謫名戍，編伍瞿塘衛。

translations.literal: A special edict demoted Ming to garrison service, enrolling him in the ranks at the Qutang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict demoted Ming to garrison service and enrolled him in the ranks at the Qutang Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年釋還。

translations.literal: The next year he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was released and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 屢薦終不復召。

translations.literal: Though repeatedly recommended, in the end he was never summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Though repeatedly recommended, he was never summoned back to office.

sentences.zh: 家居二十余年，奉親孝。

translations.literal: He dwelt at home for more than twenty years and served his parents with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for more than twenty years, dutifully caring for his parents.

sentences.zh: 親歿，與弟臺廬於墓。

translations.literal: When his parents died, he and his younger brother built mourning huts at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: After his parents died, he and his younger brother built mourning huts by their tomb.

sentences.zh: 免喪，疾作，卒。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, illness came on, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 黃直，字以方，金溪人。

translations.literal: Huang Zhi, style name Yifang, was a native of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhi, courtesy name Yifang, was from Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 受業於王守仁。

translations.literal: He received instruction from Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Wang Yangming.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年會試，主司發策極詆守仁之學。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing second-year metropolitan examination, the chief examiner set a policy question that bitterly denounced Shouren's learning.
translations.idiomatic: At the metropolitan examination of the second year of Jiajing, the chief examiner set a policy question that fiercely attacked Wang Yangming's teachings.

sentences.zh: 直與同門歐陽德不阿主司意，編修馬汝驥奇之，兩人遂中式。

translations.literal: Zhi and his fellow student Ouyang De did not curry favor with the chief examiner's intent; Compiler Ma Ruji regarded them as extraordinary, and the two men thereupon passed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and his fellow student Ouyang De refused to cater to the examiner's bias; Compiler Ma Ruji was impressed by them, and both passed the examination.

sentences.zh: 直既成進士，即疏陳隆聖治、保聖躬、敦聖孝、明聖鑒、勤聖學、務聖道六事。

translations.literal: Once Zhi had become a presented scholar, he at once memorialized setting forth six matters: exalting sagely governance, preserving the sage person, deepening sagely filial piety, clarifying sagely discernment, being diligent in sagely learning, and devoting himself to the sagely Way.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Zhi had passed the palace examination, he memorialized on six themes: exalting sagely governance, safeguarding the emperor's person, deepening imperial filial piety, clarifying imperial judgment, pursuing sagely learning, and devoting the court to the sagely Way.

sentences.zh: 除漳州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor of Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以漳俗尚鬼，盡廢境內淫祠，易其材以葺橋梁、公廨。

translations.literal: Because Zhang custom honored ghosts, he abolished every licentious shrine within the jurisdiction and converted their timber to repair bridges and government offices.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhangzhou custom was steeped in spirit worship, he abolished every improper shrine in the prefecture and used their timber to repair bridges and government offices.

sentences.zh: 御史誣以罪，送吏部降用。

translations.literal: A censor falsely charged him with a crime, and he was sent to the Ministry of Personnel for demotion.
translations.idiomatic: A censor framed him on false charges, and the Ministry of Personnel demoted him.

sentences.zh: 行至中途，疏請早定儲貳。

translations.literal: When he had gone halfway on the road, he memorialized asking that the heir apparent be settled early.
translations.idiomatic: Midway on his journey, he submitted a memorial urging the early designation of an heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，遣緹騎逮問。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sent brocade-clad guards to seize and interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and sent the imperial guard to seize and interrogate him.

sentences.zh: 無何得釋，貶沔陽判官。

translations.literal: Before long he was released, and was demoted to assistant magistrate of Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was released and demoted to assistant magistrate of Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 嘗署崇陽縣事，有惠政。

translations.literal: He once acted as magistrate of Chongyang County and had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as acting magistrate of Chongyang County and won a reputation for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 外艱歸，三年不禦酒肉。

translations.literal: When his wife's father died he returned home and for three years did not partake of wine or meat.
translations.idiomatic: When his father-in-law died he went into mourning and for three years abstained from wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 服闋赴部，適名、宗明下獄。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he went to the ministry, just as Ming and Zongming were sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he reported to the ministry, just as Yang Ming and Huang Zongming had been thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 直抗疏言：「九經之首曰修身，其中曰敬大臣，體群臣。

translations.literal: Zhi submitted a forthright memorial saying: "The first of the Nine Classics says cultivate the person; among its middle themes are respect great ministers and cherish the host of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi submitted a bold memorial saying, "The first of the Nine Classics speaks of self-cultivation; among its central themes are respecting great ministers and cherishing the body of officials.

sentences.zh: 今楊名以直言置詔獄，非所以體群臣。

translations.literal: Now Yang Ming has been placed in the imperial prison for blunt speech—this is not the way to cherish the host of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yang Ming has been consigned to the imperial prison for speaking plainly—this is no way to cherish your officials.

sentences.zh: 黃宗明以論救與同罪，非所以敬大臣。

translations.literal: Huang Zongming has been punished with the same crime for pleading in defense—this is not the way to respect great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongming has been punished equally for pleading on Ming's behalf—this is no way to respect your senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 二者未盡，天下後世疑陛下修身之道亦有所未盡矣。」

translations.literal: If these two matters are not fully achieved, all under Heaven and later ages will suspect that Your Majesty's Way of cultivating the person also has something not yet fully achieved."
translations.idiomatic: If these two duties remain unfulfilled, the realm and posterity will suspect that Your Majesty's own path of self-cultivation is likewise incomplete."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，並下詔獄拷掠，命發極邊，編戍雷州衛。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, sent them together to the imperial prison for beating and torture, ordered them dispatched to the farthest border, and enrolled them for garrison at the Leizhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, had them both thrown into the imperial prison and tortured, ordered them sent to the farthest frontier, and enrolled them for garrison duty at the Leizhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 赦還，貧甚，妻紡織以給朝夕，直讀書談道自如。

translations.literal: After amnesty he returned; he was extremely poor, and his wife spun and wove to supply morning and evening, while Zhi read books and discussed the Way as before.
translations.idiomatic: After an amnesty he returned home in dire poverty; his wife spun and wove to keep food on the table, while Zhi read and discussed the Way as calmly as ever.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: In time he died.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 郭弘化，字子弼，安福人。

translations.literal: Guo Honghua, style name Zibi, was a native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Honghua, courtesy name Zibi, was from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年進士。

translations.literal: Presented scholar in the second year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in the second year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 除江陵知縣，征授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Jiangling, then summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Jiangling, then recalled and made a censor.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，彗星見。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year a comet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eleventh year a comet appeared.

sentences.zh: 弘化言：「按《天文志》：井居東方，其宿為木。

translations.literal: Honghua said: "According to the Astronomical Treatise: Jing lies in the east, and its lodge is Wood.
translations.idiomatic: Honghua said, "According to the Astronomical Treatise, the Jing asterism lies in the east and belongs to the Wood element.

sentences.zh: 今者彗出於井，則土木繁興所致也。

translations.literal: Now the comet has issued from Jing; this is caused by the simultaneous flourishing of earth works and wood cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Now that a comet has appeared in Jing, it must be due to the simultaneous rise of earthworks and timber cutting.

sentences.zh: 臣聞四川、湖廣、貴州、江西、浙江、山西及真定諸府之采木者，勞苦萬狀。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that those gathering timber in Sichuan, Huguang, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Shanxi, and the prefectures of Zhending suffer labor in ten thousand forms.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that timber crews in Sichuan, Huguang, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Shanxi, and the prefectures around Zhending suffer every imaginable hardship.

sentences.zh: 應天、蘇、松、常、鎮五府，方有造磚之役，民間耗費不貲，窯戶逃亡過半。

translations.literal: In the five prefectures of Yingtian, Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang there is at present the work of making bricks; popular expenditure is beyond reckoning, and more than half the kiln households have fled.
translations.idiomatic: In Yingtian, Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang brick-making is under way, draining the people beyond measure, and more than half the kiln households have fled.

sentences.zh: 而廣東以采珠之故，激民為盜，至攻劫會城。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Guangdong, on account of pearl gathering, the people have been provoked into banditry, even to the point of raiding the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangdong, pearl gathering has driven the people to banditry, even to the sack of the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 皆足戾天和，幹星變。

translations.literal: All these are sufficient to violate Heaven's harmony and disturb stellar transformations.
translations.idiomatic: All of this is enough to offend Heaven's harmony and provoke celestial omens.

sentences.zh: 請悉停罷，則彗滅而前星耀矣。」

translations.literal: I ask that all be wholly halted and stopped; then the comet will vanish and the former star will shine."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that all these projects be halted entirely; then the comet will fade and the heir apparent will shine forth again."

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書許贊等請聽弘化言。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Xu Zan and others asked to heed Honghua's words.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Xu Zan and others asked the throne to heed Honghua's advice.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「采珠，故事也，朕未有嗣，以是故耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Pearl gathering is an established precedent—is it for this reason that I have no heir?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped, "Pearl gathering is an established precedent—are you saying this because I still have no heir?"

sentences.zh: 責贊等附和，黜弘化為民。

translations.literal: He blamed Zan and others for echoing him and dismissed Honghua to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuked Xu Zan and the others for echoing Honghua and stripped Honghua of office, reducing him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 久之，言官會薦，報寢。

translations.literal: After a long time the remonstrance officials jointly recommended him, but the report was buried.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval the remonstrance officials jointly recommended him, but the petition was suppressed.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 劉世龍，字元卿，慈溪人。

translations.literal: Liu Shilong, style name Yuanqing, was a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shilong, courtesy name Yuanqing, was from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年進士。

translations.literal: Presented scholar in the sixteenth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in the sixteenth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授太倉知州，改國子助教，遷南京兵部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Taicang, changed to Instructor of the National University, and promoted to Principal Clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Taicang, then made an instructor at the National University, and later promoted to a principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十三年，南京太廟災。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing the Southern Capital Imperial Ancestral Temple suffered fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing fire destroyed the imperial ancestral temple in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 世龍應詔陳三事：

translations.literal: Shilong, responding to an edict, set forth three matters:
translations.idiomatic: Shilong, responding to an imperial edict, set forth three proposals:

sentences.zh: 一、杜諂諛以正風俗。

translations.literal: First, cut off flattery to rectify custom.
translations.idiomatic: First, cut off flattery to rectify public morals.

sentences.zh: 天下風俗之不正，由於人心之壞。

translations.literal: That customs under Heaven are not correct comes from the corruption of people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The corruption of public morals stems from the corruption of men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 人心之壞，患得患失使然也。

translations.literal: The corruption of people's hearts is caused by worrying over gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts grow corrupt because men fret over gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 今天下刻薄相尚，變詐相高，諂媚相師，阿比相倚。

translations.literal: Now under Heaven harshness is mutually honored, deceit is mutually exalted, flattery is mutually taught, and factional clinging is mutually relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Today harshness is prized, deceit is admired, flattery is taught from man to man, and cliques lean on one another.

sentences.zh: 仕者日壞於上，學者日壞於下，彼倡此和，靡然成風。

translations.literal: Those in office daily worsen above, scholars daily worsen below; one leads and another harmonizes, and it spreads like wind.
translations.idiomatic: Officials grow worse by the day above, scholars below them follow suit, and one voice leads until the whole court sways together.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下赫然矯正，勿以詭隨阿比者為賢，勿以正直骨鯁者為不肖，勿以私好有所賞，勿以私惡有所罰，虛心以防邪佞，謙受以來忠讜，更敕大小臣工，協恭圖治，無權勢相軋，朋黨相傾，則風俗正矣。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty awesomely corrects this—do not regard the evasive and faction-clinging as worthy, do not regard the upright and stubborn as unworthy, do not reward according to private liking, do not punish according to private dislike, keep an open mind to guard against evil flatterers, receive humbly to draw in loyal blunt counsel, further command great and small officials to work together in governance, let no power crush another, let no faction overturn another—then custom will be rectified.
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty corrects this with authority—if you do not treat the evasive and cliquish as worthy, if you do not treat the upright and outspoken as unworthy, if you neither reward private favorites nor punish private dislikes, if you keep an open mind against flatterers and humbly welcome loyal remonstrance, and if you further command all officials to work together for good government without power crushing power or factions overturning factions—then public morals will be set right.

sentences.zh: 二、廣容納以開言路。

translations.literal: Second, broaden acceptance to open the path of speech.
translations.idiomatic: Second, broaden tolerance to open the path of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨禦之初，犯顏敢諫之臣比先朝為盛，所言或傷於激切，而放逐既久，悔悟日深。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Your Majesty's assumption of rule, ministers who risked your countenance and dared remonstrate were more numerous than in the former dynasty; what they said sometimes wounded by being too sharp, yet after long exile their repentance grows daily deeper.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of your reign, officials who dared speak bluntly to your face were more numerous than under the previous emperor; their words sometimes cut too deep, yet after long exile their repentance grows deeper by the day.

sentences.zh: 當宥其既往，以次錄用，死者則恤之。

translations.literal: You ought to pardon their past, employ them in order of precedence, and for the dead extend condolence.
translations.idiomatic: You should pardon their past offenses, restore them to office in due order, and grant posthumous honors to the dead.

sentences.zh: 仍令大小臣工直言時政，以作忠義之氣。

translations.literal: Still command great and small officials to speak plainly on current affairs, so as to rouse the spirit of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: And command all officials to speak plainly on current affairs, so as to revive the spirit of loyal service.

sentences.zh: 三、慎舉動以存大體。

translations.literal: Third, be cautious in conduct to preserve the great body of state.
translations.idiomatic: Third, be cautious in your conduct to preserve the dignity of the throne.

sentences.zh: 立國者，在敬大臣，不遺故舊。

translations.literal: In establishing a state, what matters is respecting great ministers and not abandoning old associates.
translations.idiomatic: To sustain a state one must respect great ministers and not cast aside old associates.

sentences.zh: 蓋任之既重，則禮之宜優。

translations.literal: For once the charge is weighty, courtesy ought rightly to be generous.
translations.idiomatic: Once responsibility is heavy, courtesy ought to be generous in turn.

sentences.zh: 今或忽然去之，忽然召之，甚至嬰三木，被箠楚，何以勵臣節哉！

translations.literal: Now sometimes they are suddenly removed, suddenly summoned back, even to the point of wearing the three woods and suffering beating with rods—how can this encourage the integrity of ministers!
translations.idiomatic: Yet now ministers are suddenly dismissed and suddenly recalled, even shackled and beaten with rods—how can this encourage steadfast service!

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為陛下歷試之余，其人果無足取，則宜以禮使退。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks that after Your Majesty has tested them over time, if the man truly has nothing worth taking, then he ought to be made to withdraw by ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe that after you have tested a man, if he truly proves unfit, he should be dismissed with proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 如素行無缺，偶以一時喜怒，輒從而顛倒之，陛下固付之無心，而天下有以窺陛下也。

translations.literal: If his conduct has long been without fault, yet on a moment's anger or pleasure you at once overturn him, Your Majesty may indeed set it aside without intent, yet all under Heaven will have means to peer into Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: But if a man of blameless record is suddenly overturned by a passing mood, Your Majesty may think it nothing, yet the realm will learn to read your temper.

sentences.zh: 至如張延齡憑寵為非，法難容假。

translations.literal: As for Zhang Yanling, relying on favor to do wrong, the law can hardly indulge him.
translations.idiomatic: As for Zhang Yanling, who abuses imperial favor to do wrong, the law can scarcely indulge him.

sentences.zh: 側聞長老之言，孝宗時待之過厚，遂釀今日之禍。

translations.literal: I have overheard elders say that in the Xiaozong era he was treated too generously, and so brewed today's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard elders say that Emperor Xiaozong treated him too generously, and so brewed today's disaster.

sentences.zh: 顧區區腐鼠，何足深惜！

translations.literal: Yet this petty rotten rat—what is there to cherish deeply!
translations.idiomatic: But this petty creature is scarcely worth such anguish!

sentences.zh: 獨念孝廟在天之靈，太皇太后垂老之景，乃至不能自庇其骨肉，於情忍乎？

translations.literal: I think alone of the spirit of the Xiaozong temple in Heaven and the scene of the Grand Empress Dowager in her declining years, yet unable even to shelter her own flesh and bone—in feeling, can this be borne?
translations.idiomatic: I think only of Emperor Xiaozong's spirit in Heaven and of the Grand Empress Dowager in her old age, unable even to protect her own kin—in human feeling, can this be borne?

sentences.zh: 恐陛下孝養兩宮，亦不能不為一動心也。

translations.literal: I fear that in Your Majesty's filial nurture of the two palaces, you also cannot but be moved in some measure.
translations.idiomatic: Surely in your filial care for the two palaces you too cannot remain unmoved.

sentences.zh: 頃創造神禦閣、啟祥宮，特令大臣督理其事。

translations.literal: Recently in constructing the Shenyu Pavilion and Qixiang Palace, ministers were specially ordered to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, in building the Shenyu Pavilion and Qixiang Palace, you specially ordered great ministers to supervise the work.

sentences.zh: 臣以為南京太廟方被災，工役之急當無過此。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks that since the Nanjing Imperial Ancestral Temple has just suffered disaster, no labor ought to be more urgent than this.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that with the Nanjing ancestral temple just destroyed by fire, no work ought to take precedence over its rebuilding.

sentences.zh: 今興作頻年，四方雕敝，正時絀舉贏之會，亦宜量酌緩急而為之以漸。

translations.literal: Now construction has been frequent for years, the four quarters are carved and exhausted; this is just the moment when thrift in want and display in plenty apply—one ought also to weigh urgency and ease and carry things out gradually.
translations.idiomatic: Construction has gone on for years while the realm lies exhausted; this is precisely the time to practice thrift in hardship rather than extravagance in plenty, weighing what is urgent and proceeding step by step.

sentences.zh: 此皆應天以實之道也。

translations.literal: These are all the Way of responding to Heaven with substance.
translations.idiomatic: All of this is the way to respond to Heaven with deeds, not words.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝震怒，謂世龍訕上庇逆。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was shaken with rage and said Shilong had insulted the sovereign and shielded a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was shaken with rage and declared that Shilong had insulted the throne and shielded a traitor.

sentences.zh: 械系至京，下詔獄拷掠。

translations.literal: He was shackled and brought to the capital, sent down to the imperial prison for beating and torture.
translations.idiomatic: He was shackled and brought to the capital, then thrown into the imperial prison and tortured.

sentences.zh: 獄具，復廷杖八十，斥為民。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, he was again given eighty blows in court and expelled to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was concluded, he was given eighty blows at court and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 張延齡者，昭聖太后弟也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanling was the younger brother of Empress Zhaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanling was the younger brother of Empress Zhaosheng.

sentences.zh: 帝必欲殺之，故世龍重得罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was determined to kill him; therefore Shilong offended deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was determined to have him executed, and so Shilong's offense was treated with especial severity.

sentences.zh: 後二年，又以大猾劉東山訐告，盡斥諸刑曹郎羅虞臣、徐申等，猶以延齡故也。

translations.literal: Two years later, again on the false accusation of the great villain Liu Dongshan, all the clerks of the penal offices such as Luo Yuchen and Xu Shen were wholly expelled—still on account of Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, on the false accusation of the great scoundrel Liu Dongshan, every penal-office clerk, including Luo Yuchen and Xu Shen, was driven from office—again because of the Zhang Yanling affair.

sentences.zh: 世龍家居五十年，自養親一肉外，蔬食終身。

translations.literal: Shilong dwelt at home for fifty years; apart from one portion of meat to nourish his parents, he ate vegetables all his life.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong lived in retirement for fifty years, eating vegetables all his life except for the meat he served his parents.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，族人為治衣冠葬之。

translations.literal: On the day he died, clansmen prepared his cap and robes and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died, his clansmen prepared his burial garments and laid him to rest.

sentences.zh: 徐申，字周翰，昆山人。

translations.literal: Xu Shen, style name Zhouhan, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shen, courtesy name Zhouhan, was from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，由鄉舉除蘄水知縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, through the provincial recommendation he was appointed magistrate of Qishui.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing he entered office through the provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Qishui.

sentences.zh: 改知上鐃，征授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was changed to magistrate of Shangrao and summoned to appointment as Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Shangrao, then recalled and made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 延齡之系獄也，申奏記尚書聶賢、唐龍言：「太后春秋高，延齡旦暮戮，何以慰太后心？

translations.literal: When Yanling was imprisoned, Shen submitted a note to Ministers Nie Xian and Tang Long saying: "The Empress Dowager's years are advanced; if Yanling is executed morning or evening, how can the Empress Dowager's heart be comforted?
translations.idiomatic: When Yanling was imprisoned, Shen wrote to Ministers Nie Xian and Tang Long saying, "The Empress Dowager is advanced in years; if Yanling is put to death at any moment, how can her heart be comforted?

sentences.zh: 宜援議貴議親例請於帝。」

translations.literal: You ought to cite the precedents of debating the noble and debating kin and petition the emperor."
translations.idiomatic: You should cite the precedents for sparing the noble and sparing kin and petition the emperor accordingly."

sentences.zh: 賢等深然之，獄久不決。

translations.literal: Xian and the others deeply approved, and the case long went undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Xian and the others strongly agreed, and the case dragged on unresolved.

sentences.zh: 始延齡下獄，提牢主事沈椿不令入獄，置別所。

translations.literal: At first when Yanling entered prison, Prison Director Shen Chun would not let him enter the jail and placed him in a separate site.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanling was first imprisoned, Prison Director Shen Chun refused to put him in the main jail and housed him elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 繼者益寬假之，脫梏堣，通家人出入。

translations.literal: His successors were still more lenient toward him, removed the cangue, and allowed his family to come and go.
translations.idiomatic: His successors were still more lenient, removed his shackles, and allowed his family free access.

sentences.zh: 會大猾劉東山亦系獄，上告延齡有不軌謀。

translations.literal: It happened that the great villain Liu Dongshan was also imprisoned; he reported upward that Yanling had an unorthodox plot.
translations.idiomatic: Then the great scoundrel Liu Dongshan was also imprisoned and accused Yanling of plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 憾前主事羅虞臣笞己，因訐及椿等。

translations.literal: Bearing resentment that the former director Luo Yuchen had beaten him with the rod, he therefore implicated Chun and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing a grudge because the former director Luo Yuchen had beaten him, he implicated Shen Chun and the others as well.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，命執先後提牢主事三十七人付詔獄搒掠，申與焉。

translations.literal: The emperor was shaken with rage and ordered the seizure of the thirty-seven successive prison directors, sent to the imperial prison for beating and torture, Shen among them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered all thirty-seven successive prison directors seized and tortured in the imperial prison, Shen among them.

sentences.zh: 獄具，當輸贖還職，帝命杖之廷，盡謫外任，而斥虞臣為民。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, they were due to redeem punishment and return to office; the emperor ordered them beaten at court, wholly demoted to outer posts, and expelled Yuchen to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was concluded they were sentenced to redeem their punishment and return to office, but the emperor ordered them beaten at court, sent them all to posts outside the capital, and stripped Luo Yuchen of office entirely.

sentences.zh: 虞臣，廣東順德人。

translations.literal: Yuchen was a native of Shunde in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchen was from Shunde in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部主事。

translations.literal: He served as Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 好剛疾惡。

translations.literal: He loved firmness and hated evil.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern and hated wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 既歸，結廬山中，讀書纂述。

translations.literal: After he returned, he built a hut in the mountains, read books, and compiled writings.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he built a hut in the mountains, where he read and wrote.

sentences.zh: 年僅三十五卒。

translations.literal: He died at only thirty-five years.
translations.idiomatic: He died at only thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 申既謫官，不赴，歸與同里魏校、方鳳輩優遊歗詠為樂。

translations.literal: After Shen was demoted in office, he did not go; he returned and with his fellow townsman Wei Xiao, Fang Feng, and others wandered at ease, whistling and chanting for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: After Shen was demoted he refused the new appointment and went home, where he and his townsman Wei Xiao, Fang Feng, and others passed their days in leisurely poetry and song.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: In time he died.

sentences.zh: 曾孫應聘，字伯衡，少有才名。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Yingpin, style name Boheng, in youth had a reputation for talent.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Xu Yingpin, courtesy name Boheng, won an early reputation for talent.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in the eleventh year of the Wanli reign (1583).

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor and was appointed a reviewing compiler.

sentences.zh: 二十一年京察，中蜚語當謫，拂衣歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year at the capital evaluation he fell victim to rumor and was due for demotion; he shook out his robes and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the twenty-first-year capital personnel review, malicious gossip marked him for demotion, and he resigned in disgust and went home.

sentences.zh: 座主沈一貫當國，數招之，不出。

translations.literal: His patron Shen Yiguan held power in the state and repeatedly summoned him, but he did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: His examination patron Shen Yiguan was directing affairs of state and summoned him repeatedly, yet he refused to return to office.

sentences.zh: 家居十余年，始起行人司副。

translations.literal: He lived at home for more than ten years, then was first raised as Vice Director of the Bureau of Envoys.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a decade in retirement, he was at last recalled as deputy director of the Bureau of Envoys.

sentences.zh: 遷尚寶司丞，再遷太仆少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Seal Office, and again transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to deputy director of the Imperial Seal Office and then to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 張選，字舜舉。

translations.literal: Zhang Xuan, style name Shunju.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuan, courtesy name Shunju.

sentences.zh: 黃正色，字士尚。

translations.literal: Huang Zhengse, style name Shishang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhengse, courtesy name Shishang.

sentences.zh: 皆無錫人。

translations.literal: Both were men of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Both were natives of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 同登嘉靖八年進士。

translations.literal: Both together passed the jinshi in the eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Both passed the metropolitan examinations in the eighth year of the Jiajing reign (1529).

sentences.zh: 正色除仁和知縣，選知蕭山縣，又鄰境也。

translations.literal: Zhengse was appointed magistrate of Renhe; Xuan was magistrate of Xiaoshan — again neighboring jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengse was appointed magistrate of Renhe, while Xuan governed Xiaoshan — neighboring counties as well.

sentences.zh: 選治蕭山有聲。

translations.literal: Xuan's governance of Xiaoshan had a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan won a strong reputation governing Xiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 十二年冬，先入為戶科給事中。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twelfth year he first entered as supervising secretary of the Household Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twelfth year (1533), he was the first to enter the capital as a supervising secretary in the Household Section of the Office of Scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 明年四月時享太廟，遣武定侯郭勛代。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the next year at the seasonal offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun was dispatched as substitute.
translations.idiomatic: The following April, at the seasonal sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the emperor sent the Marquis of Wuding, Guo Xun, to officiate in his stead.

sentences.zh: 選上言：「宗廟之祭，惟誠與敬。

translations.literal: Xuan memorialized above: "The sacrifices of the ancestral temple depend only on sincerity and reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan memorialized the throne: "Sacrifice at the ancestral temple rests solely on sincerity and reverence.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『吾不與祭，如不祭』。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'When I do not take part in the sacrifice, it is as though there were no sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'If I do not participate in the sacrifice, it is as though no sacrifice were held at all.'

sentences.zh: 傳曰：『神不歆非類』。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: 'Spirits do not enjoy what is not their kind.'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes commentary says, 'Spirits do not accept offerings from those who are not their kindred.'

sentences.zh: 孟春廟享，遣官暫攝，中外臣心知非得已。

translations.literal: At the spring temple offering of the first month, dispatching an official as temporary proxy — ministers within and without knew it could not be helped.
translations.idiomatic: When the first-month temple offering was entrusted to a substitute, every official at court knew the emperor had no real choice.

sentences.zh: 茲孟夏祫享，倘更不親行，則跡涉怠玩。

translations.literal: Now at this early-summer joint offering, if again he does not personally go, then the trace involves negligence and laxity.
translations.idiomatic: But if at this early-summer combined sacrifice Your Majesty again fails to attend in person, the court will read it as neglect and indifference.

sentences.zh: 如或聖體初復，未任趨蹌，宜明詔禮官先期告廟。

translations.literal: If perchance the sacred person has just recovered and is not equal to hurried obeisance, it is fitting to issue a clear edict that the ritual officials beforehand announce to the temple.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty's health has only just returned and you are not yet fit for the rushed courtesies of sacrifice, you should issue an explicit edict instructing the ritual officers to announce the circumstance to the temple in advance.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦宜靜處齋宮，以通神貺。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty also ought quietly to dwell in the fasting palace, to communicate with the divine blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should also withdraw in quiet to the fasting palace, there to commune with the spirits through purification."

sentences.zh: 帝閱疏大怒，下之禮部。

translations.literal: The Emperor, reading the memorial, was greatly angered, and sent it down to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read the memorial, he flew into a rage and referred it to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尚書夏言等言：「代祭之文，載之《周官》。

translations.literal: Minister Xia Yan and others said: "The text on proxy sacrifice is recorded in the Offices of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xia Yan and his colleagues replied: "Provisions for sacrifice by proxy appear in the Offices of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 《語》曰：『子之所慎齋戰疾』。

translations.literal: The Analects says: 'What the Master took care in was fasting, war, and sickness.'
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says, 'What the Master treated with the utmost care were fasting, war, and illness.'

sentences.zh: 疾當慎，無異於祭，選言非是。

translations.literal: Sickness ought to be treated with care, no different from sacrifice; Xuan's words are not correct.
translations.idiomatic: Illness demands the same scrupulous attention as sacrifice; Zhang Xuan is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 但小臣無知，惟陛下曲赦。」

translations.literal: But this petty official is ignorant; may Your Majesty mercifully pardon."
translations.idiomatic: Yet this junior official spoke out of ignorance — we beg Your Majesty to grant him lenient forgiveness."

sentences.zh: 帝愈怒，責言等黨比。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew still angrier, and rebuked Yan and the rest for factional collusion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still angrier and accused Yan and his colleagues of forming a clique.

sentences.zh: 命執選闕下，杖八十。

translations.literal: He ordered Xuan seized below the palace gate and beaten eighty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhang Xuan seized at the palace gate and beaten eighty strokes with the heavy rod.

sentences.zh: 帝出禦文華殿聽之，每一人行杖畢，輒以數報。

translations.literal: The Emperor came out to preside over the Wenhua Hall and listen; each time one stroke was completed, he immediately had the count reported.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself came out to the Wenhua Hall to watch; after each stroke, a runner reported the tally aloud.

sentences.zh: 杖折者三。

translations.literal: The rods that broke numbered three.
translations.idiomatic: Three beating rods snapped in the course of it.

sentences.zh: 曳出，已死。

translations.literal: He was dragged out — already dead.
translations.idiomatic: When they dragged him away, he was already dead.

sentences.zh: 帝怒猶未釋。

translations.literal: The Emperor's anger still was not released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's rage still had not subsided.

sentences.zh: 是夕，不入大內，繞殿走，制《祭祀記》一篇。

translations.literal: That evening, he did not enter the inner palace, but walked circling the halls, composing one piece "Record of Sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: That night he refused to enter the inner palace; he paced the halls in agitation and drafted a "Record on Sacrificial Rites."

sentences.zh: 一夕鋟成，明旦分賜百官。

translations.literal: In one night it was carved for printing; at dawn the next day it was distributed and bestowed on the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: It was carved for printing overnight, and at dawn the next day copies were distributed to the entire bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 而選出，家人投良劑得甦，帝竟削選籍。

translations.literal: Yet Xuan had been taken out; his family applied a good remedy and he revived, but the Emperor ultimately struck Xuan from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had been carried off, but his family administered an effective restorative and he revived — though in the end the emperor still struck him from the official registers.

sentences.zh: 選居職甫三月，遽以言得罪，名震海內。

translations.literal: Xuan had held office only three months when abruptly he offended by his words; his name shook the realm within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had been in office barely three months when this memorial brought him to ruin, yet his name resounded throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 正色是時方憂居。

translations.literal: Zhengse at this time was still in mourning residence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengse was still in mourning at the time.

sentences.zh: 已，補香山，旋改南海。

translations.literal: Afterward, he was assigned to Xiangshan, and soon transferred to Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posted to Xiangshan and soon transferred to Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 座主霍韜宗人橫甚，正色繩以法。

translations.literal: His patron Huo Tao's clansmen were extremely overbearing; Zhengse restrained them by law.
translations.idiomatic: The clansmen of his examination patron Huo Tao behaved with outrageous arrogance, and Zhengse held them to the law.

sentences.zh: 韜顧以為賢，豪強屏跡，縣中大理。

translations.literal: Tao on the contrary regarded him as worthy; powerful bullies withdrew their traces, and the county had great order.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Tao came rather to admire him for it; local bullies vanished from sight, and the county knew true peace.

sentences.zh: 十七年召為南京御史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was summoned as censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1538) he was summoned to serve as a censor in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 劾兵部尚書張瓚奸貪，事甚有跡。

translations.literal: He impeached Minister of War Zhang Zhan for wickedness and greed; the matter had very evident traces.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the minister of war Zhang Zhan for corruption and malfeasance, and the charges were well substantiated.

sentences.zh: 而中有「歷官藩臬，無一善狀」語，瓚言己未任藩臬。

translations.literal: Yet among these was the phrase "in successive offices as provincial governor and surveillance commissioner, not a single good deed"; Zhan said he himself had never served as provincial governor or surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: But the memorial included the line that "in every provincial post he held, not a single act was creditable," and Zhan protested that he had never served in such provincial offices.

sentences.zh: 帝以誣劾，奪俸兩月。

translations.literal: The Emperor regarded it as a false impeachment and docked two months' salary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled the impeachment slanderous and docked Zhengse two months' salary.

sentences.zh: 明年，章聖太后梓宮南葬，命正色護視。

translations.literal: The next year, when Empress Dowager Zhangsheng's coffin was buried in the south, he ordered Zhengse to supervise and guard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the empress dowager Zhangsheng's coffin was escorted south for burial, Zhengse was assigned to oversee the procession.

sentences.zh: 事竣，劾中官鮑忠、駙馬都尉崔元、禮部尚書溫仁和所過納饋遺。

translations.literal: When the affair ended, he impeached the eunuch Bao Zhong, the Commandant-escort Cui Yuan, and Minister Wen Renhe for accepting gifts along the route.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission concluded, he impeached the eunuch Bao Zhong, the imperial son-in-law Cui Yuan, and the minister of rites Wen Renhe for accepting gratuities along the route.

sentences.zh: 帝召詰忠等。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned them and interrogated Zhong and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhong and the others for questioning.

sentences.zh: 皆叩頭祈哀，因譖正色擅於梓宮前乘馬執扇，及江行涉險又不隨舟督護，大不敬。

translations.literal: All knocked their heads begging mercy, and thereby slandered Zhengse for on his own authority riding a horse and holding a fan before the coffin-palace, and also on the river journey facing danger yet not following the boats to supervise and guard — greatly disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: They all kowtowed in pleading and in turn accused Zhengse of arrogantly riding horseback and wielding a fan before the empress's coffin, and of failing to accompany the boats and supervise the escort when the procession faced danger on the river — charges of gross disrespect.

sentences.zh: 帝遂發怒，立捕下詔獄搒掠，遣戍遼東。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon erupted in anger, immediately seized and sent down to the imperial prison for beating and torture, and dispatched to garrison in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then flew into a rage, had Zhengse seized at once and thrown into the imperial prison for interrogation under torture, and banished him to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 正色與選初同誌相友善，至是先後以直節顯。

translations.literal: Zhengse and Xuan from the first shared the same aspiration and were friendly; by this time both successively became famed for straight integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengse and Xuan had been close friends united from the start in the same moral purpose; by now both had won fame, one after the other, for uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 正色居戍所三十年，其顛躓窮困視選尤甚。

translations.literal: Zhengse dwelt at the garrison place thirty years; his ups and downs and impoverishment surpassed Xuan's still more.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengse spent thirty years in exile, and his reverses and poverty were even more severe than Xuan's.

sentences.zh: 穆宗初，起選通政參議，以年老予致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Muzong, Xuan was raised as vice commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; because of old age he was granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Longqing reign, Xuan was recalled as vice commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and, on grounds of age, granted retirement.

sentences.zh: 召正色為大理丞，進少卿，尋遷南京太仆卿，亦引年致仕。

translations.literal: Zhengse was summoned as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, promoted to vice minister, and soon transferred to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing; he too cited age and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengse was recalled as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, promoted to vice minister, and soon made minister of the imperial stud at Nanjing; he too retired citing his years.

sentences.zh: 選先卒，正色後數年卒。

translations.literal: Xuan died first; Zhengse died several years later.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan died first; Zhengse followed him to the grave several years later.

sentences.zh: 包節，字元達，先世嘉興人，其父始遷華亭。

translations.literal: Bao Jie, style name Yuanda, his forebears were men of Jiaxing; his father first moved to Huating.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Jie, courtesy name Yuanda, came from a Jiaxing family; his father was the first to settle in Huating.

sentences.zh: 節祖鼎，池州知府。

translations.literal: Jie's grandfather Ding was prefect of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ding had served as prefect of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 為治清簡，早歲乞休，為鄉邑所重。

translations.literal: His governance was clear and simple; in early years he requested retirement and was respected by the villages and towns.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was marked by simplicity and restraint; he retired while still young and was held in high esteem in his home region.

sentences.zh: 節生五歲而孤，母躬教育之。

translations.literal: Jie was orphaned at five years; his mother personally educated him.
translations.idiomatic: Jie lost his father at five; his mother educated him herself.

sentences.zh: 登嘉靖十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the eleventh year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in the eleventh year of the Jiajing reign (1532).

sentences.zh: 授東昌推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor at Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 入為御史。

translations.literal: He entered as censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was brought into the capital as a censor.

sentences.zh: 劾兵部尚書張瓚貪穢。

translations.literal: He impeached Minister of War Zhang Zhan for greedy defilement.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the minister of war Zhang Zhan for corruption.

sentences.zh: 出按雲南。

translations.literal: He went out to inspect Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched on an inspection tour of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 時仕者以荒僥憚不欲往，因設告就遠方之法。

translations.literal: At the time officeholders because of the wilderness and peril feared and did not wish to go, so they established a law for petitioning to take distant posts.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at the time feared the region's remoteness and hardship and shunned assignments there, so the court devised a rule allowing men to petition for distant posts.

sentences.zh: 節言：「此曹誌甘投荒，非年迫衰遲，則家貧急祿。

translations.literal: Jie said: "These people are minded gladly to cast themselves into the wilds — if not because age presses and they are declining, then because the family is poor and urgently needs salary.
translations.idiomatic: Jie argued: "These men are eager to volunteer for the frontier — not because they are aged and infirm, but because they are poor and desperate for an official salary.

sentences.zh: 誌在為己，豈在恤民？

translations.literal: Their aim lies in serving themselves — how could it lie in caring for the people?
translations.idiomatic: Their motive is self-interest, not concern for the people.

sentences.zh: 滇中長吏所以多不得人也。

translations.literal: This is why the senior officials of Dianzhong so often fail to obtain the right men.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Yunnan's senior administrators so often prove inadequate.

sentences.zh: 請自今以附近選人充之，而州縣佐貳始用此曹，庶吏治可舉。」

translations.literal: I request that from now on men chosen from nearby be appointed to fill these posts, and that these people only begin to be used as assistant deputies in prefectures and counties — then perhaps local administration can be raised up."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that henceforth nominees from nearer provinces fill these posts, and that such petitioners be assigned only to secondary county and prefectural posts — only then can local governance improve."

sentences.zh: 吏部請以節言概行於雲、貴、兩廣。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel requested to apply Jie's words comprehensively in Yunnan, Guizhou, and the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel asked to apply Jie's proposal across Yunnan, Guizhou, and the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 以疾歸。

translations.literal: He returned home because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to retire.

sentences.zh: 起故官，再按湖廣。

translations.literal: He was raised to his former office and again inspected Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to his former rank and sent on a second inspection tour of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 顯陵守備中官廖斌擅威福，節欲繩之，語先泄。

translations.literal: The eunuch Liao Bin, guardian of the Xianling mausoleum, usurped authority and blessings; Jie wished to restrain him by law, but the words leaked beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Bin, the eunuch charged with guarding the Xianling mausoleum, abused his power extravagantly; when Jie prepared to discipline him, word leaked out in advance.

sentences.zh: 斌俟節謁陵時，故獻膳羞，遽使撤去，詭稱節麾出之。

translations.literal: Bin waited until Jie came to pay respects at the tomb, deliberately offered food delicacies, then hastily had them removed, falsely claiming Jie had waved them away.
translations.idiomatic: Bin waited until Jie came to perform rites at the tomb, then deliberately presented ritual offerings only to have them whisked away at once, falsely claiming that Jie had ordered them removed.

sentences.zh: 鐘祥民王憲告斌黨庇奸豪周章等，節捕章，斃之杖下。

translations.literal: The Zhongxiang commoner Wang Xian reported that Bin's party shielded the wicked powerful Zhou Zhang and others; Jie arrested Zhang and beat him to death under the rod.
translations.idiomatic: A Zhongxiang commoner named Wang Xian accused Bin's faction of sheltering the bully Zhou Zhang; Jie arrested Zhang and beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 斌益怒，遂奏節不以正旦謁陵，次日始謁，時當進膳，不旁立，褻慢大不敬。

translations.literal: Bin grew still angrier and thereupon memorialized that Jie did not visit the tomb on New Year's Day but only the next day visited; when it was time to present food he did not stand to the side — irreverent and disrespectful in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, enraged, memorialized that Jie had failed to attend the tomb on New Year's Day, appearing only the day after, and that when food was to be presented he had not stood respectfully aside — charges of gross disrespect.

sentences.zh: 奏已入，節始奏斌前事。

translations.literal: The memorial had already entered when Jie at last memorialized on Bin's prior conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's memorial had already reached the throne when Jie at last submitted his own charges against Bin.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，以節抵罪，逮詣詔獄搒掠，永戍莊浪衛。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered, made Jie answer for the crime, seized and sent to the imperial prison for beating and torture, permanently garrisoned at Zhuanglang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, held Jie answerable, had him seized and tortured in the imperial prison, and banished him permanently to Zhuanglang Guard.

sentences.zh: 莊浪極邊，敗屋頹垣，節處之甚安。

translations.literal: Zhuanglang was the extreme border; ruined houses and crumbling walls — Jie dwelt there very much at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanglang lay on the empire's outermost frontier, amid ruined hovels and crumbling walls — yet Jie made himself quite at home.

sentences.zh: 獨念其母，自傷不克終養，日飲泣。

translations.literal: Only he thought of his mother, wounded himself that he could not complete her support to the end, and daily drank tears.
translations.idiomatic: He thought only of his mother, grieved that he could not support her in her last years, and wept every day.

sentences.zh: 母訃至，晝夜哭。

translations.literal: When news of his mother's death arrived, he wept day and night.
translations.idiomatic: When word of her death arrived, he wept without cease, day and night.

sentences.zh: 已，又聞弟孝卒，撫膺曰：「誰代吾奉祀者？」

translations.literal: Afterward, he again heard his younger brother Xiao had died; he clutched his breast and said: "Who will replace me in performing the sacrifices?"
translations.idiomatic: Later he learned that his younger brother Xiao had also died; clutching his chest he cried, "Who will now tend our family's ancestral rites?"

sentences.zh: 哭益悲。

translations.literal: His weeping grew still more sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: His grief grew only deeper.

sentences.zh: 病死，遺言以衰绖殮。

translations.literal: He died of illness; his final words were to be enshrouded in mourning hemp.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness, leaving instructions to be enshrouded in the hemp mourning garments he had never been able to wear for his mother.

sentences.zh: 孝，字元愛，後節三年成進士。

translations.literal: Xiao, style name Yuan'ai, three years after Jie became jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiao, courtesy name Yuan'ai, passed the metropolitan examinations three years after Jie.

sentences.zh: 由中書舍人為南京御史。

translations.literal: From Hanlin Drafting Attendant he became Nanjing censor.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from Hanlin drafting attendant, he became a censor in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 疏論禮部尚書溫仁和主辛丑會試有奸弊，且劾庶子童承敘、贊善郭希顏、編修袁煒，帝皆不問。

translations.literal: In a memorial he discussed Minister Wen Renhe's presiding over the xinchou metropolitan examination having wicked malpractices, and moreover impeached Erudite Tong Chengxu, Companion Guo Xiyan, and Compiler Yuan Wei — the Emperor all did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the minister of rites Wen Renhe had overseen corruption in the xinchou metropolitan examination, and impeached the erudite Tong Chengxu, the companion Guo Xiyan, and the compiler Yuan Wei — the emperor ignored every charge.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又劾巡撫孫襘、吳瀚，瀚罷去。

translations.literal: Before long, he again impeached Grand Coordinators Sun Gui and Wu Han; Han was dismissed and left.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he impeached the grand coordinators Sun Gui and Wu Han; Wu Han was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 孝兄弟分居南北臺，並著風采，又皆有至情。

translations.literal: The brothers Jie and Xiao dwelt separately at the northern and southern censorate platforms, both showing striking presence, and both also had utmost familial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Bao Jie and Bao Xiao served on the northern and southern censorate circuits respectively, each distinguished for moral courage, and each possessed of deep filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 節官北不得養母，孝遂以侍養歸。

translations.literal: Jie held office in the north and could not support his mother; Xiao thereupon returned to attend and support her.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jie's northern posting kept him from caring for their mother, Xiao resigned to tend her at home.

sentences.zh: 母亡，哀毀骨立，未終喪卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died, his grief ruined him until only bones remained; before the mourning period ended he died.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, his mourning reduced him to skin and bone; he died before the mourning period had run its course.

sentences.zh: 節亦繼殞。

translations.literal: Jie also followed in death.
translations.idiomatic: Jie died soon afterward as well.

sentences.zh: 時並稱其孝。

translations.literal: At the time they were together praised for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: At the time both were celebrated for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 謝廷蒨，字子佩，富順人。

translations.literal: Xie Ting, style name Zipei, a man of Fushun.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ting, courtesy name Zipei, was a native of Fushun.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the eleventh year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in the eleventh year of the Jiajing reign (1532).

sentences.zh: 除新喻知縣，征授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Xinyu; summoned and appointed supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Xinyu, then summoned to the capital as a supervising secretary in the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 御史胡鰲言：「京師優倡雜處。

translations.literal: Censor Hu Ao said: "In the capital, actors and entertainers are mixed together in residence.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Hu Ao memorialized: "In the capital, actors and courtesans mingle everywhere.

sentences.zh: 請敕五城，諸非隸教坊兩院者，斥去之。」

translations.literal: I request an imperial command to the Five Wards that all who are not subordinate to the Two Academies of the Music Office be expelled and removed."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty instruct the Five Ward offices to expel all performers not registered with the official music academies."

sentences.zh: 都御史王廷相等議可。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Wang Tingxiang and others discussed and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief Wang Tingxiang and his colleagues endorsed the proposal.

sentences.zh: 帝惡熬言褻，謫鹽城丞，奪廷相等俸。

translations.literal: The emperor hated Ao's irreverent words, demoted him to assistant magistrate of Yancheng, and stripped Wang Tingxiang and the others of their salaries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense at Hu Ao's irreverent memorial and demoted him to assistant magistrate of Yancheng, while also suspending the salaries of Wang Tingxiang and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 廷蒨救之，被詔切責。

translations.literal: Ting pleaded on his behalf and received a stern imperial rebuke by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ting spoke up in his defense and was sharply rebuked by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 雷震謹身殿，疏陳修省數事，語直。

translations.literal: Lightning struck the Hall of Self-Cultivation; he memorialized setting forth several matters for reform and self-examination; his language was blunt.
translations.idiomatic: When lightning struck the Hall of Self-Cultivation, he submitted a memorial urging several measures of reform and self-examination, and his language was blunt.

sentences.zh: 帝摘疏中訛字，停其俸。

translations.literal: The emperor picked out erroneous characters in the memorial and suspended his salary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor seized on mistaken characters in the memorial and suspended his salary.

sentences.zh: 十八年偕同官曾烶，李逢、周充諫帝南巡，忤旨。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, together with his colleagues Zeng Dian, Li Feng, and Zhou Chong, he admonished the emperor against the southern tour, running counter to the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of the reign, together with his colleagues Zeng Dian, Li Feng, and Zhou Chong, he remonstrated against the emperor's southern tour and ran afoul of the throne.

sentences.zh: 已，給事中戴嘉猷馳疏請回鑾，而車駕已發。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, the supervising secretary Dai Jiayou rushed a memorial asking that the imperial carriage turn back, but the imperial procession had already set out.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the supervising secretary Dai Jiayou sent an urgent memorial begging that the imperial carriage turn back, but the procession had already departed.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 甫還，即執嘉猷並廷蒨等下詔獄，謫廷蒨雲南典史。

translations.literal: As soon as he returned, he had Jiayou seized together with Ting and the others and sent down to the imperial prison; Ting was demoted to registrar in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he returned when Dai Jiayou was seized, together with Xie Ting and the others, and cast into the imperial prison; Ting was demoted to county registrar in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 屢遷浙江僉事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred, eventually to vice commissioner in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred repeatedly and eventually rose to vice commissioner in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 以侍養歸，遂不出。

translations.literal: He returned home to attend his parents and thereafter did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to care for his parents and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，起故官山西，俄擢河南右參議，皆不拜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing he was recalled to his former post in Shanxi; soon he was promoted to right vice commissioner in Henan, but he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing he was recalled to his former post in Shanxi, and soon afterward was promoted to right vice commissioner in Henan, but he declined both appointments.

sentences.zh: 吏部高其行，請得以新秩歸老，許之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel praised his conduct and requested that he be allowed to retire with his new rank; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel praised his conduct and asked that he be permitted to retire with his new rank; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 萬歷改元，四川巡撫曾省吾奏言：「廷氵茝隱居三十年，家徒四壁，樂道著書，宜特加京秩，風勵士林。」

translations.literal: At the change to the Wanli reign, Zeng Shengwu, governor of Sichuan, memorialized: "Ting氵茝 has lived in seclusion for thirty years; his house holds nothing but bare walls; devoted to the Way, he writes books. He should be specially granted a capital rank to encourage the scholarly class."
translations.idiomatic: When the Wanli reign began, Zeng Shengwu, governor of Sichuan, memorialized: "Xie Ting has lived in retirement for thirty years, his home empty but for bare walls; devoted to the Way, he writes books. He ought to receive a special capital appointment to encourage the scholarly class."

sentences.zh: 詔即加進太仆少卿。

translations.literal: An edict at once promoted him to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: An edict immediately promoted him to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 又數年卒。

translations.literal: Several years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he died.

sentences.zh: 王與齡，字受甫，寧鄉人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuling, style name Shoufu, a man of Ningxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuling, courtesy name Shoufu, was a native of Ningxiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in the eighth year of the Jiajing reign (1529).

sentences.zh: 授蘇州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部主事，調吏部，進員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered service as a director in the Ministry of Revenue, was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and advanced to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as a director in the Ministry of Revenue, was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 二十一年遷文選郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to director of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of the reign he was made director of the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 澄清銓敘，所推薦皆廉靜老成。

translations.literal: He clarified appointment procedures; all whom he recommended were upright, quiet, and seasoned.
translations.idiomatic: He brought clarity to appointments and promotions, and everyone he recommended was upright, steady, and seasoned in office.

sentences.zh: 大學士翟鑾為禮部主事張惟一求吏部，嚴嵩為監生錢可教求東陽知縣，俱書抵與齡。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhai Luan asked the Ministry of Personnel on behalf of Director Zhang Weiyi of the Ministry of Rites; Yan Song asked on behalf of probationer Qian Kejiao for the post of magistrate of Dongyang — both sent letters to Yuling.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhai Luan wrote to Yuling on behalf of Zhang Weiyi, a director in the Ministry of Rites, and Yan Song wrote on behalf of the student Qian Kejiao for the magistracy of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 與齡偕員外郎吳伯亨、主事李大魁、周鈇，白之尚書許贊，具疏以聞。

translations.literal: Yuling, together with Vice Director Wu Bohang and Directors Li Dakui and Zhou Fu, reported to Minister Xu Zan and jointly submitted a memorial to inform the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yuling, together with Vice Director Wu Bohang and Directors Li Dakui and Zhou Fu, reported the matter to Minister Xu Zan, and they jointly submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 言：「平時請屬甚多。

translations.literal: They wrote: "In normal times requests for favoritism are very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: They wrote: "Petitions for private favor are countless in ordinary times.

sentences.zh: 臣等違抗，積罪如山。

translations.literal: We have resisted them, and our accumulated offenses are mountain-high.
translations.idiomatic: We have resisted them, and our accumulated offenses stand mountain-high.

sentences.zh: 非聖明覆庇，則二權奸主於中，群鷹犬和於外，臣等不為前選郎王嘉賓之斥，得為近日御史謝瑜之罷，幸矣。」

translations.literal: Were it not for Your Sagely Brightness sheltering us, then the two powerful schemers would hold sway within while hawks and hounds harmonize without — we would not have escaped dismissal like the former selection director Wang Jiabin, nor would we have been as lucky as the recent censor Xie Yu, who was merely dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: Were it not for Your Sagely Majesty's protection, the two powerful schemers would rule within while their hawks and hounds worked in concert without — we would not have escaped dismissal like the former selection director Wang Jiabin, nor been as fortunate as the recent censor Xie Yu, who was merely removed from office."

sentences.zh: 疏入，鑾言惟一資望應遷。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Luan said Weiyi's qualifications and standing warranted promotion.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Luan argued that Weiyi's qualifications and standing warranted promotion.

sentences.zh: 嵩抵無致書事，請逮可教訊治，因言：「聖明日覽奏章，革弊厘奸悉宸斷。

translations.literal: Song denied having sent any letter and asked that Kejiao be seized and interrogated, adding: "Your Sagely Brightness reads memorials daily; reforming abuses and sorting out traitors are entirely the sovereign's own decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Song denied ever having written such a letter and asked that Kejiao be seized and interrogated, adding: "Your Sagely Majesty reads memorials every day and reforms abuses and roots out traitors entirely by Your own judgment.

sentences.zh: 而贊等妄意臣輩為之，借以修怨。

translations.literal: Yet Zan and the others falsely suppose that we did it, using this to nurture old resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zan and the others wrongly suppose that we did this, using the charge to settle old scores.

sentences.zh: 然贊柔良，第受制所屬耳。」

translations.literal: Yet Zan is mild and good — he is only controlled by his subordinates."
translations.idiomatic: Zan himself is mild and upright; he is only controlled by his subordinates."

sentences.zh: 帝方信嵩，又見疏中引嘉賓、瑜事，遂發怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was then trusting Song, and seeing the memorial cite the cases of Jiabin and Yu, he thereupon flew into a rage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then inclined to trust Song, and when he saw the memorial cite the cases of Jiabin and Yu, he flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 切責贊，除與齡名，伯亨等俱調外。

translations.literal: He sharply rebuked Zan, struck Yuling's name from the registers, and transferred Bohang and the others to posts outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He sharply rebuked Zan, struck Yuling's name from the registers, and transferred Bohang and the others to posts outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 給事中周怡論之，廷杖系獄。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Zhou Yi argued on their behalf and was beaten at court and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Zhou Yi spoke up for them and was beaten at court and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 御史徐宗魯等亦以為言，皆奪俸。

translations.literal: The censors Xu Zonglu and others also spoke on the matter; all had their salaries confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The censors Xu Zonglu and others also remonstrated, and all had their salaries suspended.

sentences.zh: 自是，諸司以與齡為戒，無復敢與嵩抗。

translations.literal: From then on, all offices took Yuling as a warning and none again dared oppose Song.
translations.idiomatic: From then on every office took Yuling as a warning, and none dared oppose Yan Song again.

sentences.zh: 與齡既罷，錦衣遣使偵其裝，襆被外無長物，稱嘆而去。

translations.literal: After Yuling's dismissal, the Embroidered-Uniform Guard sent men to spy on his baggage; beyond a wrapped quilt he had no long possessions; they exclaimed in admiration and left.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuling's dismissal, the Embroidered-Uniform Guard sent men to inspect his baggage; apart from a wrapped quilt he owned nothing of value, and they departed exclaiming in admiration.

sentences.zh: 裏居，角巾躬稼圃，翛然自得。

translations.literal: Living at home, he wore a plain kerchief and worked his fields himself, utterly content.
translations.idiomatic: At home he wore a scholar's kerchief and worked his own fields, utterly at ease.

sentences.zh: 郡人為作《平陽四賢詩》美之。

translations.literal: Men of the commandery composed "Poems on the Four Worthies of Pingyang" in praise of him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of his commandery composed the "Poems on the Four Worthies of Pingyang" in his praise.

sentences.zh: 四賢者，尚書韓文、陶琰、張潤及與齡也。

translations.literal: The four worthies were Ministers Han Wen, Tao Yan, Zhang Run, and Yuling.
translations.idiomatic: The four worthies were the ministers Han Wen, Tao Yan, Zhang Run, and Yuling.

sentences.zh: 越二十余年，卒。
