translations.literal: More than twenty years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty years later he died.

sentences.zh: 周鈇，字汝威，榆次人。

translations.literal: Zhou Fu, style name Ruwei, a man of Yuci.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu, courtesy name Ruwei, was a native of Yuci.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in the fifth year of the Jiajing reign (1526).

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，巡按陜西。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor and sent as touring inspector to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor and sent to inspect Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 被俘民自塞外逃歸者，邊將殺以冒功。

translations.literal: Captured civilians who had escaped from beyond the border were killed by frontier generals to claim merit.
translations.idiomatic: Civilians who had been captured and escaped back from beyond the border were killed by frontier generals so they could claim merit.

sentences.zh: 鈇請下詔嚴禁，有報降五人以上者賞之。

translations.literal: Fu requested an edict strictly forbidding this, with reward for reporting five or more who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Fu asked that an edict strictly forbid this and reward anyone who reported five or more who had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 再按山東，特改右春坊清紀郎兼翰林院侍書。

translations.literal: On a second tour of Shandong, he was specially appointed Right Subinstructor for Pure Records in the Eastern Palace, concurrently Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: On a second inspection tour of Shandong he was specially appointed Right Subinstructor for Pure Records in the Eastern Palace, with concurrent duty as Hanlin reader-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 俺答將入寇，總督侍郎翟鵬以聞。

translations.literal: Altan was about to invade; Governor Vice Minister Zhai Peng reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan Khan was about to invade, the grand coordinator Zhai Peng reported the threat.

sentences.zh: 鈇以中樞無籌策，請早為計。

translations.literal: Fu said the central administration had no strategy and asked that plans be made early.
translations.idiomatic: Fu said the central government had no strategy in place and urged that plans be made at once.

sentences.zh: 帝以為浮詞亂政，責降廬州府知事。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded this as empty words disturbing government and punished him with demotion to clerical officer in Luzhou prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regarded this as empty talk that disturbed government and demoted him to clerical officer in the Luzhou prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 旋改國子監丞，擢吏部文選主事。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to vice director of the Directorate of Education, then promoted to director of the Bureau of Appointments in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice director of the Directorate of Education, then promoted to director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 坐與齡發嵩等私屬事，貶河間通判。

translations.literal: Because of his role in exposing Song and others' private favoritism, he was demoted to assistant prefect of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had joined Yuling in exposing Yan Song's private patronage, he was demoted to assistant prefect of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 已而吏部擬擢南京吏部主事。

translations.literal: Later the Ministry of Personnel proposed promoting him to director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Ministry of Personnel proposed promoting him to director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 嵩言鈇調官甫四月，不得驟遷。

translations.literal: Song said Fu had been transferred only four months and could not be suddenly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Song objected that Fu had held his new post only four months and could not be promoted so quickly.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，詰責尚書許贊等，令錄左降官遷擢者姓名。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, rebuked Minister Xu Zan and the others, and ordered a record of the names of demoted officials who had been promoted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, rebuked Minister Xu Zan and the others, and ordered a list of demoted officials who had nonetheless been promoted.

sentences.zh: 贊引罪，並列陳叔頤等十六人以聞。

translations.literal: Zan acknowledged guilt and listed Chen Shuyi and fifteen others in a memorial to inform the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zan accepted blame and memorialized with a list of Chen Shuyi and fifteen others.

sentences.zh: 詔奪贊等俸，鐫文選郎鄭曉三級，鈇、叔頤等褫職為民。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Zan and the others of salary, cut the Bureau of Appointments director Zheng Xiao three grades, and dismissed Fu, Shuyi, and the others to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: An edict suspended the salaries of Zan and his colleagues, reduced Bureau of Appointments Director Zheng Xiao three grades, and stripped Fu, Shuyi, and the others of office, making them commoners.

sentences.zh: 廷臣論薦鈇，以嵩在位，不復召。

translations.literal: Court officials repeatedly recommended Fu, but with Song still in power he was never recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials repeatedly recommended Fu, but while Yan Song remained in power he was never recalled.

sentences.zh: 穆宗初，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the start of Muzong's reign, he was posthumously enfeoffed as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Muzong's reign he was posthumously granted the title of vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 楊思忠，字孝夫，平定人。

translations.literal: Yang Sizhong, style name Xiaofu, a man of Pingding.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sizhong, courtesy name Xiaofu, was a native of Pingding.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twentieth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in the twentieth year of the Jiajing reign (1541).

sentences.zh: 歷禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He served through the post of supervising secretary in the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the post of supervising secretary in the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，孝烈皇后大祥。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the great mourning period for Empress Xiaolie ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year the great mourning period for Empress Xiaolie came to an end.

sentences.zh: 欲預祧仁宗，附後太廟，下廷議。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to move Emperor Renzong ahead in the ancestral line and install him in the Rear Temple; the matter was sent to court for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to move Emperor Renzong ahead in the ancestral line and install him in the Rear Temple, and the matter was referred to court for discussion.

sentences.zh: 尚書徐階以為非禮，思忠力贊階議，余人莫敢言。

translations.literal: Minister Xu Jie held this contrary to ritual; Sizhong strongly backed Jie's view, and the others did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xu Jie held that this was contrary to ritual, and Sizhong strongly backed his view while the others dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 帝使人覘知狀。

translations.literal: The emperor sent men to observe and learn the situation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent men to observe what was happening.

sentences.zh: 及議上，嚴旨譙責，命階與思忠更定，二人復據禮對。

translations.literal: When the discussion was submitted, a stern edict reproached them and ordered Jie and Sizhong to reconsider; the two again responded according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When the discussion was submitted, a stern edict rebuked them and ordered Jie and Sizhong to reconsider; the two again answered according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，竟祧仁宗。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier and ultimately moved Renzong ahead in the line.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still angrier and in the end moved Emperor Renzong ahead in the ancestral line.

sentences.zh: 階故得帝眷，獨銜思忠。

translations.literal: Jie still enjoyed the emperor's favor, but he alone bore resentment against Sizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jie still enjoyed the emperor's favor, but he alone harbored resentment against Sizhong.

sentences.zh: 每當遷，輒報罷。

translations.literal: Whenever Sizhong was due for promotion, the report would be rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever promotion was proposed for him, the report was rejected.

sentences.zh: 逾三年，正旦日食，陰雲不見，六科合疏賀。

translations.literal: More than three years later, on New Year's Day an eclipse occurred but clouds hid it; the Six Sections jointly submitted a congratulatory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: More than three years later, on New Year's Day there was an eclipse, but clouds hid it from view, and the Six Sections jointly submitted a congratulatory memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝摘疏中語，詰為不成文，曰：「思忠懷欺，不臣久矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor picked phrases from the memorial and questioned them as ill-formed prose, saying: "Sizhong has harbored deceit and has long been disloyal."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor seized on phrases in the memorial and challenged them as ill-formed prose, saying: "Sizhong has long harbored deceit and has been disloyal for years."

sentences.zh: 杖百，斥為民，余皆奪俸。

translations.literal: He was beaten a hundred strokes and dismissed to commoner status; the others all had their salaries confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: He was beaten a hundred strokes, dismissed to commoner status, and the others all had their salaries suspended.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年起掌吏科。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing he was recalled to head the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing he was recalled to head the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 三遷右僉都御史，巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: Promoted three times to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted three times to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 五年改南京戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to right vice minister of revenue in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made right vice minister of revenue in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 致仕卒。

translations.literal: He retired from office and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office and died.

sentences.zh: 世宗晚年，進言者多得重譴。

translations.literal: In the late years of the Shizong reign, those who offered remonstrance often suffered heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the late years of Emperor Shizong's reign, those who remonstrated often suffered severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，俺答薄都城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Altan pressed close to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Altan Khan pressed close to the capital.

sentences.zh: 通政使樊深陳禦寇七事，中言仇鸞養寇要功。

translations.literal: Communications Commissioner Fan Shen set forth seven matters for repelling invaders, among them that Qiu Luan had nurtured the raiders to claim merit.
translations.idiomatic: Communications Commissioner Fan Shen set forth seven measures for repelling the invaders, among them the charge that Qiu Luan had nurtured the raiders in order to claim merit.

sentences.zh: 帝方眷鸞，立斥為民。

translations.literal: The emperor was then favoring Luan and immediately dismissed Fan to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then favoring Luan and immediately dismissed Fan to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 四十二年正月，御史淩儒請重貪墨之罰，革虛冒之兵，搜遺佚之士。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-second year, Censor Ling Ru asked for heavier penalties for corruption, elimination of phantom troops, and search for overlooked talent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the forty-second year, Censor Ling Ru asked for heavier penalties for corruption, the elimination of phantom troops on the rolls, and a search for overlooked talent.

sentences.zh: 因薦羅洪先、陸樹聲、吳嶽、吳悌。

translations.literal: He therefore recommended Luo Hongxian, Lu Shusheng, Wu Yue, and Wu Ti.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Luo Hongxian, Lu Shusheng, Wu Yue, and Wu Ti.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其市恩，杖六十，除名。

translations.literal: The emperor hated this as currying favor and beat him sixty strokes and struck his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated this as an attempt to curry favor, had him beaten sixty strokes, and struck his name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 四十五年十月，御史王時舉劾刑部尚書黃光升，言：「內官季永以訴事犯乘輿，本無死比，乃擬真犯；

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the forty-fifth year, Censor Wang Shiju impeached Minister of Punishments Huang Guangsheng, saying: "The eunuch Ji Yong, who sued over a matter and offended the imperial carriage, had no statute warranting true execution, yet was sentenced as a capital offender;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the forty-fifth year, Censor Wang Shiju impeached Huang Guangsheng, minister of punishments, saying: "The eunuch Ji Yong, who brought a lawsuit and in doing so offended the imperial carriage, had no statute warranting execution as a true capital offender, yet was sentenced as one;

sentences.zh: 奸人王相私閹良民者三，本無生法，乃擬矜疑。

translations.literal: the villain Wang Xiang privately castrated three good commoners, for which there was no law permitting life, yet doubtful clemency was applied.
translations.idiomatic: the villain Wang Xiang privately castrated three innocent commoners, for which there was no law permitting life, yet doubtful clemency was applied.

sentences.zh: 宜勒令致仕。」

translations.literal: Huang should be ordered to retire."
translations.idiomatic: Huang ought to be ordered to retire from office."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命編氓口外。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and ordered him registered as a commoner and exiled beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered him registered as a commoner and exiled beyond the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 逾月，御史方新上言：「黃河與北狄之患，自古有之。

translations.literal: A month later, Censor Fang Xin memorialized: "The troubles of the Yellow River and the northern barbarians have existed since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, Censor Fang Xin memorialized: "The troubles of the Yellow River and the northern barbarians have existed since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 乃今豐、沛間陸地為渠，而興都有陵寢之憂，鳳陽有冰雹之厄，河南有饑饉之災，堯之洚水不烈於此矣。

translations.literal: Yet now between Feng and Pei the dry land has become a channel, while Xingdu has anxiety over imperial tombs, Fengyang has the calamity of hail, and Henan has famine — Yao's flood waters were not more violent than this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now the dry land between Feng and Pei has become a channel, Xingdu faces anxiety over the imperial tombs, Fengyang has suffered hail, and Henan faces famine — the flood waters of Yao's age were not more violent than this.

sentences.zh: 諸邊將惰卒驕，寇至輒巽忄耎觀望，而寧武有軍士之變，南贛有土兵之叛，徽州諸府有礦徒竊發之虞，舜之三苗不棘於此矣。

translations.literal: Frontier generals are slack and troops arrogant; when bandits arrive they are timid and irresolute and watch from afar, while Ningwu had mutiny of troops, southern Gan had revolt of native soldiers, and the prefectures of Huizhou had fear of mining ruffians rising — Shun's Sanmiao were not more troublesome than this.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier generals are slack and troops arrogant; when raiders arrive they shrink back and watch from afar, while Ningwu has seen mutiny among the troops, southern Gan has seen native soldiers rebel, and the Huizhou prefectures face the threat of mining ruffians rising in secret — the Three Miao of Shun's age were not more troublesome than this.

sentences.zh: 夫洚水、三苗不足為累者，以堯、舜兢業於上，而禹、臯諸臣分憂於下也。

translations.literal: That flood and Sanmiao did not weigh heavily was because Yao and Shun were diligent above, while Yu, Gao Yao, and other ministers shared the cares below.
translations.idiomatic: That flood and the Three Miao did not prove overwhelming was because Yao and Shun were diligent above, while Yu, Gao Yao, and the other ministers shared the cares below.

sentences.zh: 今司論納者日獻禎祥，而疆場之臣，惟冒首功，隱喪敗。

translations.literal: Now those who remonstrate daily present auspicious omens, while frontier officials only claim heads for merit and conceal defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Today those who remonstrate daily present auspicious omens, while frontier officials only claim heads for merit and conceal their defeats.

sentences.zh: 為國分憂者，誰也？

translations.literal: Who shares the cares for the state?
translations.idiomatic: Who now shares the state's burdens?

sentences.zh: 斥罰之法，今不得不嚴。

translations.literal: The law of dismissal must now be made strict.
translations.idiomatic: The law of dismissal must now be made strict.

sentences.zh: 而陛下亦宜隨事自責，痛加修省，然後災變可息，而外患可弭也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should also blame yourself according to each matter and earnestly reform; then prodigies may cease and external troubles be quelled."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should also blame yourself for each matter and reform with utmost earnestness; only then may prodigies cease and external troubles be quelled."

sentences.zh: 疏入，斥為民。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, he was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, he was dismissed to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 深，大同人。

translations.literal: Shen was a man of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shen was a native of Datong.

sentences.zh: 儒，泰州人。

translations.literal: Ru was a man of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Ru was a native of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 時舉，順天通州人。

translations.literal: Shiju was a native of Tongzhou in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiju came from Tongzhou in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 新，青陽人。

translations.literal: Xin was a native of Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xin came from Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 穆宗嗣位，並復官。

translations.literal: When the Muzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, all had their offices restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Muzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, all had their offices restored.

sentences.zh: 深尋遷刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Shen was soon transferred to Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shen was soon promoted to Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 齊康之劾徐階也，深劾康並詆高拱。

translations.literal: When Qi Kang impeached Xu Jie, Shen impeached Kang and also slandered Gao Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Kang impeached Xu Jie, Shen impeached Kang and also attacked Gao Gong.

sentences.zh: 時登極詔書赦死罪以下囚，而流徒已至配者，所司拘律令不遣。

translations.literal: At the time the accession edict pardoned prisoners below the death penalty, but for exiles and convicts already at their places of banishment, the responsible offices clung to statutes and regulations and would not release them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the accession edict pardoned prisoners below the death penalty, but for exiles and convicts already at their places of banishment, the responsible offices clung to statutes and would not release them.

sentences.zh: 深言殊死猶赦，而此反不及，非所以廣皇仁。

translations.literal: Shen said that even those deserving death were pardoned, yet these were not included—this is not how to extend imperial benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Shen argued that even those deserving death were pardoned, yet these were not included—this was not how to extend imperial benevolence.

sentences.zh: 詔從其議。

translations.literal: An edict followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed his proposal.

sentences.zh: 旋進左侍郎，罷歸。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Left Vice Minister, then dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Left Vice Minister, then dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 儒既復御史，益發舒，亦以康事率同列劾拱。

translations.literal: After Ru had his censor's post restored, he became all the more unrestrained; he also led his colleagues in impeaching Gong over the Kang affair.
translations.idiomatic: After Ling Ru had his censor's post restored, he became all the more unrestrained; he also led his colleagues in impeaching Gao Gong over the Kang affair.

sentences.zh: 拱罷，又劾去大學士郭樸。

translations.literal: When Gong was dismissed, he again impeached and drove out Grand Secretary Guo Pu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Gong was dismissed, he again impeached and drove out Grand Secretary Guo Pu.

sentences.zh: 頃之，劾罷撫治鄖陽都御史劉秉仁。

translations.literal: Before long he impeached and removed Liu Bingren, Censor-in-Chief administering Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he impeached and removed Liu Bingren, the censor-in-chief administering Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 又以永平失事劾總督劉燾、巡撫耿隨卿、總兵官李世忠罪。

translations.literal: He also impeached Governor Liu Tao, Grand Coordinator Geng Suiqing, and Regional Commander Li Shizhong for the Yongping disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Governor Liu Tao, Grand Coordinator Geng Suiqing, and Regional Commander Li Shizhong for the Yongping disaster.

sentences.zh: 隨卿、世忠被逮，燾貶官。

translations.literal: Suiqing and Shizhong were arrested; Tao was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Suiqing and Shizhong were arrested; Tao was demoted.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年，儒再遷右僉都御史，理山西屯鹽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing, Ru was again transferred to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and administered the Shanxi garrison salt.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longqing, Ru was again promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and administered the Shanxi garrison salt.

sentences.zh: 吏部追論其知永豐時貪墨，遂落職閑住。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel pursued charges of his corruption when he was magistrate of Yongfeng; he was thereupon stripped of office and lived in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel pursued charges of corruption from his time as magistrate of Yongfeng; he was stripped of office and lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 時舉復官後，巡按貴州。

translations.literal: After Shiju had his office restored, he toured and inspected Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his office was restored, Wang Shiju served as touring censor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 聞給事中石星廷杖，且帝方廣市珠寶，馳疏救星，極陳奢靡之害。

translations.literal: Hearing that the supervising secretary Shi Xing had been beaten at court, and that the emperor was then greatly expanding the market in pearls and jewels, he hurriedly memorialized to save Xing and set forth at length the harm of extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the supervising secretary Shi Xing had been beaten at court while the emperor was greatly expanding the market in pearls and jewels, he hurriedly memorialized to save Xing and set forth at length the harm of extravagance.

sentences.zh: 已，請陳後還中宮。

translations.literal: Later he asked that the heir Chen be returned to the central palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked that the heir Chen be returned to the central palace.

sentences.zh: 章並報聞。

translations.literal: Both memorials were reported as received.
translations.idiomatic: Both memorials were acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，都給事中雒遵、御史景嵩、韓必顯論譚綸被謫，時舉抗章救之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, the Chief Supervising Secretary Luo Zun and the censors Jing Song and Han Bixian spoke on Tan Lun's behalf and were demoted; Shiju submitted a bold memorial to save them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign, the Chief Supervising Secretary Luo Zun and the censors Jing Song and Han Bixian spoke on Tan Lun's behalf and were demoted; Wang Shiju submitted a bold memorial to save them.

sentences.zh: 歷大理左少卿。

translations.literal: He rose to Left Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 新終湖廣參議。

translations.literal: Xin ended his career as Administrative Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xin ended his career as administrative commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：賈山有言：「忠臣之事君也，言切直則不用而身危。」

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Jia Shan once said: "When a loyal minister serves his ruler, if his words are blunt and direct they are not used and his person is endangered."
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: Jia Shan once said, "When a loyal minister serves his ruler, if his words are blunt and direct they go unheeded and his person is endangered."

sentences.zh: 「然切直之言，明主之所亟欲聞，忠臣之所蒙死而竭知也。」

translations.literal: "Yet blunt and direct words are what an enlightened ruler most urgently wishes to hear, and what a loyal minister will risk death to exhaust his knowledge in offering."
translations.idiomatic: Yet blunt and direct words are what an enlightened ruler most urgently wishes to hear, and what a loyal minister will risk death to offer with all his knowledge."

sentences.zh: 鄧繼曾諸人箴主闕，指時弊，言切直矣，而杖斥隨之。

translations.literal: Deng Jiceng and the others admonished the ruler's faults, pointed to the abuses of the time—their words were blunt and direct—yet beating and dismissal followed.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jiceng and his fellows admonished the ruler's faults and pointed to the abuses of the time; their words were blunt and direct, yet beating and dismissal followed.

sentences.zh: 伊尹曰：「有言逆於汝心，必求諸道。」

translations.literal: Yi Yin said: "When there are words that go against your heart, you must seek their meaning in the Way."
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin said, "When there are words that go against your heart, you must seek their meaning in the Way."

sentences.zh: 有旨哉，有旨哉！

translations.literal: How pointed the meaning! How pointed the meaning!
translations.idiomatic: How pointed the meaning! How pointed the meaning!
